This finding indicates a possible exposure of an population to RSV, a contagious human pathogen, and highlights the importance of increased surveillance at the human–wildlife interface. [10.1007/s10393-026-01837-y]

Of 3,560 participants, 2,969 (83%) had [≥]1 illness over 4,299 person-years. [10.64898/2026.10.15.26365672]
The RSVPreF vaccine was first licensed for use in pregnancy in 2023 and demonstrated efficacy in a single pivotal randomized trial (MATISSE). [10.2196/94382]

papers.title: Monoclonal Antibodies for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Infants and Children: An Updated Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Motivated by the emergence of a long-acting monoclonal antibody (clesrovimab), the availability of data from the complete MELODY trial cohort, and results from a large randomized trial (HARMONIE), we updated our prior network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of monoclonal antibodies for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants. METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials that examined the efficacy and safety of RSV infection prophylaxis with clesrovimab, motavizumab, nirsevimab, palivizumab, and suptavumab versus one another or placebo or no prophylaxis in infants. We performed a frequentist framework random-effects network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Developments and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to assess the certainty of evidence. RESULTS: Eighteen trials enrolling 33,283 infants were included. Clesrovimab (odds ratio [OR] 0.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.02-0.37, moderate certainty), motavizumab (OR 0.12; 95% CI 0.07-0.19, moderate certainty), and nirsevimab (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.34; moderate certainty) were associated with reductions in the rate of severe respiratory syncytial virus infection. Nirsevimab, motavizumab, clesrovimab, and intramuscular palivizumab were associated with reductions in RSV infection, and several agents were also associated with reduced hospitalization. Motavizumab and nirsevimab, and clesrovimab were associated with reductions in broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes. Motavizumab reduced both mechanical ventilation use and intensive care unit admission. No significant differences were found in all-cause mortality and drug-related or serious adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: This updated network meta-analysis confirmed that the effectiveness and safety of clesrovimab were comparable to those of established monoclonal antibodies. Motavizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab showed benefits for broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review evaluates the efficacy and safety of monoclonal antibodies for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants. papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Motivated by the emergence of a long-acting monoclonal antibody (clesrovimab), the availability of data from the complete MELODY trial cohort, and results from a large randomized trial (HARMONIE), we updated our prior network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of monoclonal antibodies for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants. METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials that examined the efficacy and safety of RSV infection prophylaxis with clesrovimab, motavizumab, nirsevimab, palivizumab, and suptavumab versus one another or placebo or no prophylaxis in infants. We performed a frequentist framework random-effects network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessments, Developments and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to assess the certainty of evidence. RESULTS: Eighteen trials enrolling 33,283 infants were included. Clesrovimab (odds ratio [OR] 0.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.02-0.37, moderate certainty), motavizumab (OR 0.12; 95% CI 0.07-0.19, moderate certainty), and nirsevimab (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.11-0.34; moderate certainty) were associated with reductions in the rate of severe respiratory syncytial virus infection. Nirsevimab, motavizumab, clesrovimab, and intramuscular palivizumab were associated with reductions in RSV infection, and several agents were also associated with reduced hospitalization. Motavizumab and nirsevimab, and clesrovimab were associated with reductions in broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes. Motavizumab reduced both mechanical ventilation use and intensive care unit admission. No significant differences were found in all-cause mortality and drug-related or serious adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: This updated network meta-analysis confirmed that the effectiveness and safety of clesrovimab were comparable to those of established monoclonal antibodies. Motavizumab, nirsevimab, and clesrovimab showed benefits for broader lower respiratory tract infection-related outcomes.

papers.title: Efficacy, Effectiveness, and Immunogenicity of the Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Vaccine Administered During Pregnancy: Protocol for a Living Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, with the highest burden in the first 6 months of life. Maternal immunization with the bivalent (RSV-A and RSV-B) prefusion F (RSVPreF) protein subunit vaccine (ABRYSVO) is a recently recommended strategy for preventing RSV-related outcomes in infants. First licensed for use in pregnancy in 2023, the RSVPreF vaccine demonstrated efficacy in a single pivotal randomized trial (Maternal Immunization Study for Safety and Efficacy; MATISSE); postlicensure real-world evidence on vaccine effectiveness across settings, seasons, and subgroups and on antibody durability and transplacental transfer remains limited and has not been synthesized in a continuously updated framework, motivating this review. Objective This living systematic review and meta-analysis will synthesize emerging postlicensure data on the efficacy, effectiveness, and immunogenicity of the RSVPreF vaccine in real-world settings. Methods We will conduct, in real time, a living systematic review and meta-analysis following Cochrane methods and PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols) guidance, including randomized clinical trials and postlicensure real-world studies (eg, cohort, case-control, test-negative, and quasi-experimental studies). Primary objectives are evaluation of vaccine efficacy and effectiveness in preventing RSV-specific and all-cause respiratory disease and immunogenicity in infants and pregnant individuals. Vaccine effectiveness outcomes include RSV laboratory-confirmed infection, RSV acute respiratory illness, RSV lower respiratory tract disease, RSV hospitalization, RSV complications, all-cause lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization, and antibiotic use in infants with RSV infection. Immunogenicity outcomes include maternal neutralizing antibody titers, maternal-infant transfer ratios, infant titers over time, and RSV viral load. We will search MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, Science Citation Index Expanded, Chinese biomedical and citation databases, clinical trial registries from January 2023 onward with no language restrictions, updating at least monthly. Two investigators will independently select studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias. Adjusted estimates will be standardized to vaccine efficacy and effectiveness. Certainty will be graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system. Results This living systematic review was funded in June 2025. Searches began in January 2023 and will continue with surveillance updates at least monthly until April 2028. As of January 2026, 837 records were screened, 105 (12.5%) were assessed in full text, and 12 (1.4%) met the inclusion criteria, of which 10 (1.2%) contributed extractable data. Data collection and analysis are ongoing and displayed on an interactive dashboard. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conferences, and a real-time dashboard, with the first effectiveness estimates available in July 2026. Conclusions This living systematic review and meta-analysis will provide a continuously updated synthesis of real-world evidence on maternal RSVPreF vaccination to inform clinical and policy decisions.

source_records.title: Efficacy, Effectiveness, and Immunogenicity of the Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Vaccine Administered During Pregnancy: Protocol for a Living Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, with the highest burden in the first 6 months of life. Maternal immunization with the bivalent (RSV-A and RSV-B) prefusion F (RSVPreF) protein subunit vaccine (ABRYSVO) is a recently recommended strategy for preventing RSV-related outcomes in infants. First licensed for use in pregnancy in 2023, the RSVPreF vaccine demonstrated efficacy in a single pivotal randomized trial (Maternal Immunization Study for Safety and Efficacy; MATISSE); postlicensure real-world evidence on vaccine effectiveness across settings, seasons, and subgroups and on antibody durability and transplacental transfer remains limited and has not been synthesized in a continuously updated framework, motivating this review. Objective This living systematic review and meta-analysis will synthesize emerging postlicensure data on the efficacy, effectiveness, and immunogenicity of the RSVPreF vaccine in real-world settings. Methods We will conduct, in real time, a living systematic review and meta-analysis following Cochrane methods and PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols) guidance, including randomized clinical trials and postlicensure real-world studies (eg, cohort, case-control, test-negative, and quasi-experimental studies). Primary objectives are evaluation of vaccine efficacy and effectiveness in preventing RSV-specific and all-cause respiratory disease and immunogenicity in infants and pregnant individuals. Vaccine effectiveness outcomes include RSV laboratory-confirmed infection, RSV acute respiratory illness, RSV lower respiratory tract disease, RSV hospitalization, RSV complications, all-cause lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization, and antibiotic use in infants with RSV infection. Immunogenicity outcomes include maternal neutralizing antibody titers, maternal-infant transfer ratios, infant titers over time, and RSV viral load. We will search MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, Science Citation Index Expanded, Chinese biomedical and citation databases, clinical trial registries from January 2023 onward with no language restrictions, updating at least monthly. Two investigators will independently select studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias. Adjusted estimates will be standardized to vaccine efficacy and effectiveness. Certainty will be graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system. Results This living systematic review was funded in June 2025. Searches began in January 2023 and will continue with surveillance updates at least monthly until April 2028. As of January 2026, 837 records were screened, 105 (12.5%) were assessed in full text, and 12 (1.4%) met the inclusion criteria, of which 10 (1.2%) contributed extractable data. Data collection and analysis are ongoing and displayed on an interactive dashboard. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conferences, and a real-time dashboard, with the first effectiveness estimates available in July 2026. Conclusions This living systematic review and meta-analysis will provide a continuously updated synthesis of real-world evidence on maternal RSVPreF vaccination to inform clinical and policy decisions.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿下呼吸道疾病的主要原因,在生命的前 6 个月内负担最高。该综述重点关注妊娠期间施用 RSVPreF 疫苗 预防婴儿 RSV 相关结局的功效、有效性和免疫原性。主要目标是评估 疫苗 在预防 RSV 特异性和全因呼吸道疾病方面的功效和效果,并评估婴儿和孕妇的免疫原性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查将综合有关 RSVPreF 疫苗 在现实环境中的功效、有效性和免疫原性的新出现的许可后数据。它将遵循 Cochrane 方法和 PRISMA-P 指导,包括随机临床试验和许可后真实世界研究(例如 队列研究、病例对照、测试阴性和准实验研究)。自 2023 年 1 月起,检索将在 MEDLINE、Embase、Cochrane 图书馆、LILACS、Science Citation Index Expanded、中国生物医学和引文数据库以及临床试验注册中心进行,没有语言限制,至少每月更新一次。两名研究人员将独立选择研究、提取数据并评估偏倚风险。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: RSVPreF 疫苗 于 2023 年首次获得用于妊娠的许可,并在一项关键随机试验 (MATISSE) 中证明了其有效性。关于 疫苗 在不同环境、季节和亚组中的有效性以及抗体耐久性和经胎盘转移的许可后真实世界证据仍然有限,并且尚未在持续更新的框架中综合。本综述旨在提供此类综合,为临床和政策决策提供信息。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些数据没有综合的连续框架,证据还不够全面,无法得出关于 疫苗 在不同人群或长期结果中的有效性的明确结论。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这项实时系统回顾和荟萃分析将提供关于母亲 RSVPreF 疫苗接种 的真实世界证据的不断更新的综合,为临床和政策决策提供信息。研究结果将通过同行评审的出版物、会议和实时仪表板进行传播,并于 2026 年 7 月提供第一个有效性估计。

papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

papers.title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

The research addresses the need for effective strategies to improve RSV vaccine and nirsevimab adoption in clinical settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and nirsevimab in two maternity hospitals within the Sydney Local Health District. It analysed deidentified summary data from electronic medical records on RSV immunisation status during the implementation period.
analysis.methods: Deidentified summary data from electronic medical records were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used to reflect on the rollout process.
analysis.main_results: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with the reason for refusal not recorded. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. They noted that leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and online prerecording can optimise clinician education.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform strategies for improving immunisation uptake for RSV prevention products in maternity settings, supporting the integration of such programs into routine clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on deidentified summary data and the lack of recorded reasons for nirsevimab refusal. The evidence is moderate as it provides descriptive insights into the rollout process without detailed statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rollout of the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) maternal vaccine and the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab in two maternity hospitals in Sydney, Australia. It highlights the improvement in RSV vaccination coverage among mothers from 4% in the first month to 70-74% by late 2025, alongside a decrease in the number of infants requiring nirsevimab. The authors note that 36% of eligible newborns declined nirsevimab, with reasons for refusal not documented. They identify key lessons, including the importance of multidisciplinary engagement and leveraging existing education structures to optimise clinician training. The study suggests that integrating immunisation into medical record workflows can support program adoption. However, the reliance on deidentified summary data and lack of recorded refusal reasons limit the depth of the findings, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分享快速实施 RSV 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。该研究解决了对有效策略的需求,以改善 RSV 疫苗 和 尼塞韦单抗 在临床环境中的采用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在悉尼地方卫生区的两家妇产医院推出 RSV 孕产妇 疫苗 和 尼塞韦单抗。它分析了实施期间电子病历中有关 RSV 免疫状况的去识别化摘要数据。
elements_zh.methods: 来自电子病历的去识别化摘要数据被描述性地分析为计数和比例。实施研究综合框架用于反思推出过程。
elements_zh.main_results: 两家 SLHD 医院分娩妇女的 RSV 疫苗接种 覆盖率从推出第一个月(2025 年 2 月)的 4% 提高到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,但没有记录拒绝的原因。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,让多学科领导者和临床医生参与对于协调应对和项目成功推出至关重要。他们指出,利用现有的教育结构、员工会议和在线预录音可以优化临床医生教育。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to share lessons from the rapid implementation of RSV prevention products and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. The research addresses the need for effective strategies to improve RSV vaccine and nirsevimab adoption in clinical settings.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved the rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and nirsevimab in two maternity hospitals within the Sydney Local Health District. It analysed deidentified summary data from electronic medical records on RSV immunisation status during the implementation period.
analysis_en.methods: Deidentified summary data from electronic medical records were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used to reflect on the rollout process.
analysis_en.main_results: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with the reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform strategies for improving immunisation uptake for RSV prevention products in maternity settings, supporting the integration of such programs into routine clinical practice.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on deidentified summary data and the lack of recorded reasons for nirsevimab refusal. The evidence is moderate as it provides descriptive insights into the rollout process without detailed statistical analysis.

papers.title_zh: 压力之下:从澳大利亚悉尼快速实施 呼吸道合胞病毒 孕产妇 疫苗 和婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 中吸取的经验教训。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.
papers.abstract_zh: 目标:分享悉尼地方卫生区 (SLHD) 推出 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。服务类型:推出 RSV 母体 疫苗 和用于新生儿的可注射长效单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗,以保护他们免受 RSV 感染和住院治疗。方法:以计数和比例的形式对两家 SLHD 妇产医院的 RSV 免疫状况电子病历中的去识别化汇总数据进行描述性分析。实施研究综合框架被用作反思推出过程的镜头。结果:两家 SLHD 医院分娩妇女的 RSV 疫苗接种 覆盖率从推出第一个月(2025 年 2 月)的 4% 提高到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,但没有记录拒绝的原因。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。经验教训:多学科领导者和临床医生的参与对于协调应对和计划成功推出至关重要。利用现有的教育结构、员工会议和使用在线预录音可以优化临床医生教育。新计划需要时间才能融入常规临床实践,而涉及为不同群体提供多种免疫产品的计划需要明确的信息传递和系统保障措施以防止错误。将免疫接种作为标准做法纳入医疗记录工作流程可以支持计划的采用和采用。

papers.title: Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in Black-Horned Capuchin Monkeys, Brazil.
papers.abstract: Abstract We carried out a viral surveillance study on 30 black-horned capuchin monkeys ( Sapajus nigritus ) in Rio Doce State Park, a protected area in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. Samples were tested for orthopoxviruses, flaviviruses, coronaviruses, influenza viruses, and a wide range of other respiratory viruses using molecular and serological methods. RT-qPCR detected the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) genome in oral swabs from two asymptomatic juvenile females sampled in an area with high human interaction. This finding indicates a possible exposure of an population to RSV, a contagious human pathogen, and highlights the importance of increased surveillance at the human–wildlife interface.
authors: Ana Yasha Ferreira de La Salles

papers.title: Outcomes of ‘neglected’ respiratory viruses (PIV, hMPV) vs. Influenza and RSV lower respiratory tract infections in hematologic malignancies: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viral lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) are a major cause of mortality and morbidity in adults with hematological malignancies. While influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are well-characterized, the comparative clinical burden of parainfluenza virus (PIV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) remains poorly defined. Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420251152933) following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We searched four databases from inception to October 2025 for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes of PIV/hMPV LRTI versus RSV/influenza pneumonia in adults undergoing chemotherapy for hematological malignancies. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and length of stay. Dual independent review was performed for study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). A narrative synthesis was conducted. Results From 1,071 screened records, 12 studies (11 ‘Good’ quality) comprising a total of 4,841 patients were included. Data for mechanical ventilation were particularly scarce, and notably absent for PIV and Influenza. All-cause mortality for PIV (0–16%) and hMPV (1.4%) was not higher than for influenza (2.2–33.3%) or RSV (0–25%). ICU admission rates were highly variable and overlapping across all viruses. A salient finding, derived from a single study, was a substantially prolonged median length of hospital stay for PIV (28 days) compared to RSV (18 days), hMPV (9 days), and influenza (10–13 days). Conclusion PIV and hMPV LRTI present a distinct clinical profile in this vulnerable population. While mortality is comparable to more common viruses, PIV infection was reported in a single, small-cohort study to be associated with a prolonged hospital stay, suggesting a potential morbidity burden that requires further validation. These findings challenge the perception of these pathogens as uniformly less severe and highlight an urgent need for prospective studies to guide optimized management and resource allocation.

Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420251152933) following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We searched four databases from inception to October 2025 for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes of PIV/hMPV LRTI versus RSV/influenza pneumonia in adults undergoing chemotherapy for hematological malignancies. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and length of stay. Dual independent review was performed for study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). A narrative synthesis was conducted. Results From 1,071 screened records, 12 studies (11 ‘Good’ quality) comprising a total of 4,841 patients were included. Data for mechanical ventilation were particularly scarce, and notably absent for PIV and Influenza. All-cause mortality for PIV (0–16%) and hMPV (1.4%) was not higher than for influenza (2.2–33.3%) or RSV (0–25%). ICU admission rates were highly variable and overlapping across all viruses. A salient finding, derived from a single study, was a substantially prolonged median length of hospital stay for PIV (28 days) compared to RSV (18 days), hMPV (9 days), and influenza (10–13 days). Conclusion PIV and hMPV LRTI present a distinct clinical profile in this vulnerable population. While mortality is comparable to more common viruses, PIV infection was reported in a single, small-cohort study to be associated with a prolonged hospital stay, suggesting a potential morbidity burden that requires further validation. These findings challenge the perception of these pathogens as uniformly less severe and highlight an urgent need for prospective studies to guide optimized management and resource allocation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract infections in adults with hematological malignancies, aiming to compare the clinical burden of RSV with that of parainfluenza virus (PIV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching four databases up to October 2025 for observational studies on RSV, PIV, and hMPV LRTI in adults undergoing chemotherapy for hematological malignancies; study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale, and a narrative synthesis was undertaken.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Twelve studies comprising 4,841 patients were included; mortality rates for RSV were comparable to those for influenza and PIV/hMPV (0–25% for RSV versus 0–16% for PIV, 1.4% for hMPV, and 2.2–33.3% for influenza); ICU admission rates varied but overlapped across all viruses, indicating no clear superiority of RSV in severity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Data on mechanical ventilation were scarce and absent for PIV and influenza; evidence for prolonged hospital stay was limited to a single small‐cohort study of PIV; overall heterogeneity in ICU admission rates and limited sample sizes highlight the need for more robust data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective studies are urgently required to validate the potential morbidity burden of RSV and to guide optimized management and resource allocation for patients with hematological malignancies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examined RSV lower respiratory tract infections in adults with hematological malignancies, comparing outcomes with PIV and hMPV. Twelve observational studies (4,841 patients) were included. Mortality and ICU admission rates for RSV were comparable to influenza and PIV/hMPV, with no clear evidence of greater severity. Mechanical ventilation data were scarce, and only one small study suggested a prolonged hospital stay for PIV. The heterogeneity and limited data underscore the need for prospective research to clarify RSV’s morbidity burden and inform clinical management.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 呼吸道病毒性下呼吸道感染 (LRTI) 是 死亡率 和成人血液系统恶性肿瘤发病的主要原因。虽然流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的特征已明确,但副流感病毒 (PIV) 和人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 的相对临床负担仍不清楚。方法 我们按照 PRISMA 2020 指南进行了系统评价(PROSPERO:CRD420251152933)。我们检索了四个数据库,从成立到 2025 年 10 月,进行观察性研究,比较接受血液恶性肿瘤化疗的成人中 PIV/hMPV LRTI 与 RSV/流感肺炎的临床结果。主要结局是全因 死亡率、入住 ICU、机械通气和住院时间。对研究选择、数据提取和质量评估(纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表)进行了双重独立审查。进行了叙述综合。结果 从 1,071 份筛选记录中,纳入了 12 项研究(11 项“良好”质量),总共涉及 4,841 名患者。机械通气的数据尤其稀少,尤其是 PIV 和流感的数据。PIV (0–16%) 和 hMPV (1.4%) 的全因 死亡率 不高于流感 (2.2–33.3%) 或 RSV (0–25%)。ICU 入院率差异很大,并且所有病毒都有重叠。一项研究的一个显着发现是,与 RSV(18 天)、hMPV(9 天)和流感(10-13 天)相比,PIV(28 天)的中位住院时间显着延长。结论 PIV 和 hMPV LRTI 在这一易感人群中呈现出独特的临床特征。虽然 死亡率 与更常见的病毒相当,但一项小型 队列研究 研究报告 PIV 感染与住院时间延长有关,这表明存在潜在的发病负担,需要进一步验证。这些发现挑战了人们对这些病原体普遍不那么严重的看法,并强调迫切需要进行前瞻性研究来指导优化管理和资源分配。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注患有血液系统恶性肿瘤的成人中的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 下呼吸道感染,旨在将 RSV 与副流感病毒 (PIV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 的临床负担进行比较。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 根据 PRISMA 2020 指南进行了系统评价,检索了截至 2025 年 10 月的四个数据库,以查找接受血液恶性肿瘤化疗的成人中 RSV、PIV 和 hMPV LRTI 的观察性研究;研究选择、数据提取和质量评估由两名评审员使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表独立进行,并进行了叙述综合。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 纳入了 12 项研究,涉及 4,841 名患者;RSV 的 死亡率 率与流感和 PIV/hMPV 的 死亡率 率相当(RSV 为 0–25%,PIV 为 0–16%,hMPV 为 1.4%,流感为 2.2–33.3%);所有病毒的 ICU 入院率各不相同,但有重叠,表明 RSV 在严重程度上没有明显的优势。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于 PIV 和流感的机械通气数据很少且不存在;延长住院时间的证据仅限于一项针对 PIV 的小型 队列研究 研究;ICU 入院率的总体异质性和有限的样本量凸显了对更可靠数据的需求。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 迫切需要前瞻性研究来验证 RSV 的潜在发病负担,并指导血液恶性肿瘤患者的优化管理和资源分配。

papers.title: Perceived barriers to respiratory syncytial virus vaccination and vaccination coverage among pregnant women: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Introduction.Argentina introduced maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in 2024 to prevent severe respiratory infections in infants.To ensure satisfactory vaccination rates, it is important to identify barriers to its implementation.Objective.To identify barriers to RSV vaccination among pregnant women.We estimated RSV vaccination coverage and the potential association between coverage and barriers. Population and methods.A cross-sectional study based on a survey of mothers who were eligible to receive the RSV vaccine.We developed and validated a tool to identify structural, informational, emotional, and social barriers.We used logistic regression for univariate and multivariate analyses.Results.We surveyed 216 mothers.RSV vaccine coverage was 43.7%.In the univariate analysis, fewer than 5 prenatal visits and not receiving clear information were associated with lower vaccination rates.In the multivariate analysis, knowledge of the RSV vaccine was the only factor independently associated with vaccination coverage (adjusted OR: 3.4; 95% CI: 1.9-6.2;p <0.001). Conclusion.RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women was lower than that for other vaccines recommended during pregnancy.We identified limited vaccine availability and limited knowledge about the vaccine as factors associated with non-vaccination.Strengthening information and recommendations during prenatal care could help improve vaccination coverage.This study provides a validated tool for assessing barriers to vaccination among pregnant women.

source_records.abstract: Argentina introduced maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in 2024 to prevent severe respiratory infections in infants. To ensure satisfactory vaccination rates, it is important to identify barriers to its implementation. To identify barriers to RSV vaccination among pregnant women. A cross-sectional study based on a survey of mothers who were eligible to receive the RSV vaccine. We developed and validated a tool to identify structural, informational, emotional, and social barriers. We used logistic regression for univariate and multivariate analyses. We surveyed 216 mothers. RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women was lower than that for other vaccines recommended during pregnancy. We identified limited vaccine availability and limited knowledge about the vaccine as factors associated with non-vaccination. Strengthening information and recommendations during prenatal care could help improve vaccination coverage. This study provides a validated tool for assessing barriers to vaccination among pregnant women.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 阿根廷于 2024 年引入针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的孕产妇 疫苗接种,以预防婴儿严重呼吸道感染。为了确保令人满意的 疫苗接种 率,识别其实施的障碍非常重要。目的:确定孕妇感染 RSV 疫苗接种 的障碍。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项基于对有资格接受 RSV 疫苗 的母亲的调查的横断面研究。我们调查了 216 名母亲。
elements_zh.methods: 我们开发并验证了一种工具来识别结构、信息、情感和社交障碍。我们使用逻辑回归进行单变量和多变量分析。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV 疫苗 覆盖率为 43.7%。在单变量分析中,少于 5 次产前检查和未收到明确信息与较低的 疫苗接种 率相关。在多变量分析中,RSV 疫苗 的知识是与 ZX​​QTERMKQXZ 覆盖率独立相关的唯一因素(调整后 OR:3.4;95% CI:1.9-6.2;p <0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 孕妇中 RSV 疫苗接种 的覆盖率低于怀孕期间推荐的其他 疫苗 的覆盖率。我们将有限的 疫苗 可用性和有限的 疫苗 知识确定为与非 疫苗 相关的因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 加强产前护理期间的信息和建议有助于提高 疫苗接种 的覆盖率。这项研究提供了一个经过验证的工具,用于评估孕妇 疫苗接种 的障碍。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.title: Maternal immunization with RSV-VLPs in a non-human primate model of RSV infection
papers.abstract: Using a non-human primate model, we evaluated an RSV pre-fusion F and G protein virus-like particle-based maternal immunization strategy and evaluated the effects of pregnancy on vaccine-induced immunity against RSV. Immunization during pregnancy induced robust systemic and mucosal IgG and neutralizing antibody titers. Upon post-partum challenge, this vaccination strategy enhanced humoral recall responses and Fc-effector functions, and reduced viral load in dams. Infants born to vaccinated dams had increased levels of RSV antibodies in the plasma and lung mucosa, which were correlated with reduced viral load; these infants also exhibited reduced pulmonary eosinophilia. Interestingly, vaccination during pregnancy was associated with increased post-fusion F responses and NAb titers, and we observed a reduction in viral load following post-partum challenge compared to nonpregnant controls. These results support the potential of a VLP-based maternal immunization strategy and provide insight into vaccine-induced immunity against RSV in pregnant and post-partum adults and infants.

papers.title_zh: 在 RSV 感染的非人灵长类动物模型中使用 RSV-VLP 进行母体免疫
papers.source_body_en: Using a non-human primate model, we evaluated an RSV pre-fusion F and G protein virus-like particle-based maternal immunization strategy and evaluated the effects of pregnancy on vaccine-induced immunity against RSV. Immunization during pregnancy induced robust systemic and mucosal IgG and neutralizing antibody titers. Upon post-partum challenge, this vaccination strategy enhanced humoral recall responses and Fc-effector functions, and reduced viral load in dams. Infants born to vaccinated dams had increased levels of RSV antibodies in the plasma and lung mucosa, which were correlated with reduced viral load; these infants also exhibited reduced pulmonary eosinophilia. Interestingly, vaccination during pregnancy was associated with increased post-fusion F responses and NAb titers, and we observed a reduction in viral load following post-partum challenge compared to nonpregnant controls. These results support the potential of a VLP-based maternal immunization strategy and provide insight into vaccine-induced immunity against RSV in pregnant and post-partum adults and infants.

papers.title: Cynarin Targets Host CX3CR1 for Dual-Action Prophylaxis against RSV Infection and Pulmonary Pathology
papers.abstract: Abstract Safe, small-molecule prophylactic agents against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are critically lacking. Here, we identify Cynarin, an artichoke-derived dietary polyphenol, as a micromolar affinity CX3CR1 antagonist. Mechanistically, Cynarin confers dual-action protection through two distinct routes: it acts as a “chemical shield” to competitively block viral entry at the epithelial interface by binding CX3CR1, and through a separate CX3CR1-independent mechanism, exhibits intrinsic, virus-independent anti-inflammatory properties by directly suppressing macrophage activation. This target-based interaction was rigorously validated via biochemical and functional assays. In an RSV-infected mouse model, prophylactic administration of Cynarin demonstrated superior efficacy over therapeutic treatment. It significantly reduced pulmonary viral load, ameliorated lung consolidation, and potently suppressed the RSV-induced cytokine storm. Collectively, our findings establish a novel host-directed strategy utilizing Cynarin to target CX3CR1, highlighting the translational potential of food-derived bioactives in offering a dual prophylactic safeguard against viral infection and associated pulmonary pathology.
papers.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the critical need for safe, small-molecule prophylactic agents against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) due to the lack of effective options. The research sought to identify potential compounds that could offer dual-action protection against RSV infection and associated pulmonary pathology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized an RSV-infected mouse model to evaluate the prophylactic efficacy of Cynarin. The design included both prophylactic and therapeutic treatment groups to compare outcomes.
analysis.methods: Cynarin was identified as a CX3CR1 antagonist through biochemical and functional assays. The dual-action mechanism was explored by examining its effects on viral entry and macrophage activation independently.
analysis.main_results: Prophylactic administration of Cynarin in an RSV-infected mouse model showed superior efficacy compared to therapeutic treatment. It significantly reduced pulmonary viral load, ameliorated lung consolidation, and suppressed the RSV-induced cytokine storm.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that targeting CX3CR1 with Cynarin represents a novel host-directed strategy for dual-action prophylaxis against RSV infection and pulmonary pathology, offering potential for future therapeutic development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the potential of food-derived bioactives like Cynarin in providing safe and effective prophylactic measures against RSV, which could inform future research and development of targeted therapies for viral infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an animal model, which may not fully translate to human outcomes. However, the evidence is strong due to rigorous biochemical and functional validation of Cynarin's dual-action mechanism.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies Cynarin, a dietary polyphenol derived from artichoke, as a potential dual-action prophylactic agent against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The research highlights its ability to block viral entry by acting as a CX3CR1 antagonist and to suppress inflammation through a CX3CR1-independent mechanism. In an RSV-infected mouse model, Cynarin demonstrated superior prophylactic efficacy compared to therapeutic treatment, significantly reducing viral load and lung consolidation while suppressing cytokine storms. The findings suggest a novel host-directed strategy for RSV prevention, emphasizing the translational potential of food-derived compounds. However, the study's reliance on an animal model limits its direct applicability to human contexts, though the evidence is robust due to thorough biochemical and functional validation.

papers.title_zh: Cynarin 以 宿主 CX3CR1 为靶点,针对 RSV 感染和肺部病理学进行双重预防
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Safe, small-molecule prophylactic agents against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are critically lacking. Here, we identify Cynarin, an artichoke-derived dietary polyphenol, as a micromolar affinity CX3CR1 antagonist. Mechanistically, Cynarin confers dual-action protection through two distinct routes: it acts as a “chemical shield” to competitively block viral entry at the epithelial interface by binding CX3CR1, and through a separate CX3CR1-independent mechanism, exhibits intrinsic, virus-independent anti-inflammatory properties by directly suppressing macrophage activation. This target-based interaction was rigorously validated via biochemical and functional assays. In an RSV-infected mouse model, prophylactic administration of Cynarin demonstrated superior efficacy over therapeutic treatment. It significantly reduced pulmonary viral load, ameliorated lung consolidation, and potently suppressed the RSV-induced cytokine storm. Collectively, our findings establish a novel host-directed strategy utilizing Cynarin to target CX3CR1, highlighting the translational potential of food-derived bioactives in offering a dual prophylactic safeguard against viral infection and associated pulmonary pathology.

papers.title: Impact of Low Community Circulation of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) on Immunity Debt Against RSV in Adults During the Coronavirus Disease 2019 Pandemic.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The concept of immunity debt due to reduced circulation of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in adults is controversial. We questioned whether adults lost protective antibodies when RSV was not circulating in Houston during the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) pandemic. METHODS: We studied 100 adults (mean age, 49 years; range, 21-82 years) from a longitudinal cohort: 50 SARS-CoV-2 seronegative and 50 SARS-CoV-2 infected. They were followed up from March 2020 to April 2021, when RSV was not in circulation. Three serum samples were collected per adult during the observation period and were tested for neutralizing antibodies (NtAbs) against 4 RSV/A and RSV/B strains, fusion protein (F) site competitive antibodies (CAs), and natural killer cell antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (NK ADCC). Antibody kinetics and decay were analyzed. RESULTS: Seronegative and infection groups exhibited similar geometric mean NtAb titers against RSV/A and RSV/B strains, warranting a single combined cohort. The NtAb titers against the RSV strains during the 3 visits were stable over a mean of 309 days. Comparable antibody kinetic stability and decay rates were observed for F site CAs to sites Ø, II, and IV. NK ADCC activity was detected in 29 participants with no correlation to neutralizing or F site CAs. CONCLUSIONS: We detected remarkable stability in protective antibody levels in adults against RSV when it was not circulating in Houston. Immunity debt could not be ascribed to the adult population in our cohort. We identified Fc-mediated antibody effector function by NK ADCC in a minority of adults, but this was not correlated with protective antibodies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether adults experienced immunity debt against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in Houston, when RSV was not circulating. papers.title: Interactions between respiratory viruses in US adults and children: a prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Background: The relationship between recent viral infection and subsequent susceptibility to, or protection against, other viruses remains unclear, particularly across ages and symptom status. Methods: A prospective cohort study enrolled participants aged 6 months to 49 years in Washington and Oregon, USA, 2022-2024. Weekly nasal swabs were tested for SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and influenza A/B; additional swabs were collected during symptomatic illness and were also tested for parainfluenza (PIV) 1-4, endemic human coronaviruses (hCOV), adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, human rhinovirus (hRV), and enteroviruses. Proportional hazards regression models were used to characterize associations between incident symptomatic infection (illness) and history of recent illness due to other viruses (within 1-7, 8-14, 15-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180 days), adjusted for geographic region, age, sex, daycare/school/work attendance, household size, and number of children in the household. For SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV, these analyses were repeated to study incidence of infection (including asymptomatic cases). Findings: Of 3,560 participants, 2,969 (83%) had [≥]1 illness over 4,299 person-years. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) in the short term ([≤]2 weeks) after an illness were predominantly below 1, indicating that recent viral illness was often associated with lower risk of subsequent illness with other viruses. Across age groups, recent hRV illness was associated with lower risk of hCOV, PIV, and RSV illness (aHRs 0.07-0.27). SARS-CoV-2 illness was associated with a higher short-term risk of adenovirus and PIV illness (aHRs 3.20-3.33). In children aged 6 months-4 years, recent influenza illness was associated with higher short-term risk of SARS-CoV-2 illness. Including asymptomatic infections generally attenuated these associations. Interpretation: Some viral illnesses may alter short-term susceptibility to subsequent viral illnesses. Interactions may differ by age and symptom status. Funding: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; Washington State Department of Health.

In children aged 6 months-4 years, recent influenza illness was associated with higher short-term risk of SARS-CoV-2 illness. Including asymptomatic infections generally attenuated these associations. Interpretation: Some viral illnesses may alter short-term susceptibility to subsequent viral illnesses. papers.abstract_zh: 背景:近期病毒感染与随后对其他病毒的易感性或防御能力之间的关系仍不清楚,特别是在年龄和症状状态之间。方法:一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究招募了 2022 年至 2024 年在美国华盛顿州和俄勒冈州年龄为 6 个月至 49 岁的参与者。每周对鼻拭子进行 SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和甲型/乙型流感病毒检测;在有症状的疾病期间收集了额外的拭子,并检测了副流感(PIV)1-4、地方性人类冠状病毒(hCOV)、腺病毒、人类偏肺病毒、人类鼻病毒(HRV)和肠道病毒。使用比例风险回归模型来描述事件症状感染(疾病)与其他病毒引起的近期疾病史(1-7、8-14、15-30、31-60、61-90、91-180天内)之间的关联,并根据地理区域、年龄、性别、日托/学校/工作出勤率、家庭规模和家庭儿童数量进行调整。对于 SARS-CoV-2、流感和 RSV,重复这些分析以研究感染的 发病率(包括无症状病例)。结果:在 3,560 名参与者中,2,969 名参与者 (83%) 在 4,299 人年中患有 [≥]1 种疾病。患病后短期(≤2周)内的调整后风险比(aHR)主要低于1,表明最近的病毒性疾病通常与其他病毒随后患病的风险较低相关。在各个年龄组中,近期 hRV 疾病与 hCOV、PIV 和 RSV 疾病风险较低相关(aHR 0.07-0.27)。SARS-CoV-2 疾病与腺病毒和 PIV 疾病的较高短期风险相关(aHR 3.20-3.33)。在 6 个月至 4 岁的儿童中,近期流感疾病与 SARS-CoV-2 疾病的短期风险较高相关。包括无症状感染通常会减弱这些关联。解释:某些病毒性疾病可能会改变短期内对后续病毒性疾病的易感性。相互作用可能因年龄和症状状态而异。资助:美国疾病控制与预防中心;华盛顿州卫生部。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Versus Influenza in Hospitalized Adults During the Post-Pandemic Era: Clinical Characteristics, Similarities and Discrepancies
papers.abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has emerged as a major cause of hospitalization among adults in the post-pandemic era. We studied the epidemiological findings and the outcomes of patients hospitalized with influenza or RSV during the first post-pandemic respiratory virus season in Northern Greece. Methods: This multicenter retrospective study included adults hospitalized with RSV or influenza between November 2023 and May 2024 at two hospitals in Thessaloniki, Greece. Epidemiological data, clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings, vaccination status, and clinical outcomes were retrieved and compared. Results: Twenty-seven patients with RSV and forty-eight with influenza were included. RSV patients were older (77.7 vs. 67.2 years, p < 0.01) with a higher prevalence of cardiovascular disease, chronic pulmonary disease, and malignancy, and had tachypnea more frequently at presentation (p = 0.024). No significant differences in the laboratory, radiological findings, and outcomes between the two groups were recorded. No patient was vaccinated against RSV, while 20.8% of the influenza patients had been previously vaccinated. Conclusions: RSV patients had a greater burden of comorbidities, whereas overall clinical outcomes did not significantly differ from those with influenza.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the clinical characteristics of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza in hospitalized adults during the post-pandemic era in Northern Greece. The research aimed to identify differences in patient demographics, comorbidities, and outcomes between the two viruses. A multicenter retrospective study was conducted from November 2023 to May 2024, including 27 RSV and 48 influenza patients. RSV patients were older and had a higher prevalence of comorbidities, but no significant differences in laboratory findings, radiological results, or clinical outcomes were observed. No RSV patients were vaccinated, while 20.8% of influenza patients had prior vaccination. The authors concluded that RSV presents a greater burden of comorbidities, yet overall clinical outcomes are similar to those of influenza. The study's retrospective nature and limited sample size suggest moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection: Enhanced Reactive Oxygen Species Production and Weakened Antioxidant Defenses Worsen Disease Severity
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory infections in infants and young children globally. The severity of RSV-associated diseases is often ascribed to a dysregulated immune response, characterized by increased secretion of proinflammatory proteins and ineffective T helper type 2 (Th2) cell activity. The host’s primary defense against RSV relies on a well-coordinated innate immune response initiated by resident airway epithelial cells, the first target of RSV infection. These cells respond to viral invasion by generating reactive oxygen species (ROS), activating the production of Type I and III interferons, and releasing proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Moderate levels of ROS act as key molecules that regulate antiviral signaling, enhancing the host’s ability to recognize and eliminate invading pathogens. However, severe RSV infection disrupts cellular homeostasis triggering excessive ROS production, while simultaneously weakening the host’s antioxidant defenses. This redox imbalance subverts the activity of key cellular defensive mechanisms, ultimately increasing viral replication, and worsening RSV infection severity. Modulation of oxidative stress may offer an innovative approach in managing the progression and outcome of RSV infection.

papers.title: Molecular detection of human respiratory syncytial virus using real-time RT-PCR among patients with acute respiratory tract infections at a tertiary care hospital in Kanchipuram
papers.abstract: Background: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is a major viral pathogen responsible for severe acute lower respiratory tract infection (ALRI), particularly among infants, young children, elderly individuals, and immunocompromised patients. Globally, RSV contributes substantially to paediatric morbidity and mortality, especially in low-and middle-income countries. In India, RSV-associated respiratory infections remain a public concern, with seasonal variation in viral circulation and limited regional molecular surveillance data.Aims and Objectives: To detect RSV (A & B) in patients presenting with acute respiratory tract symptoms using Real-Time RT-PCR.Materials and Methods: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted in MMCH&RI over a period of 10 months. Nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs were collected from patients with symptoms of acute respiratory tract infections. Viral RNA extraction was performed, followed by molecular detection of RSV by using Real-Time RT-PCR.Results: Out of 150 patients, the majority were < 5 years of age (52.7%), followed by adults (31.3%) and elderly individuals (16%). In this study population, there was a male predominance, with 58.7%. The most common clinical features included rhinorrhea (92.7%), cough (68%), fever (64%), and dyspnea (36%). Comorbidities were present in 37.3%, with respiratory comorbidities accounting for 12%. Out of the analyzed 150 samples, 1 (0.67%) tested positive for RSV-A.Conclusion: RSV-A was detected in 0.7% of patients with acute respiratory tract infections, providing baseline regional surveillance data from South India. Real-time RT-PCR proved effective for RSV detection and subtyping, underscoring the need for sustained molecular surveillance to better define RSV burden and guide public health strategies in India.

papers.title: Respiratory syncytial virus-induced ADAM17 activity controls maintenance of epithelial barrier integrity and promotes syncytium formation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection causes epithelial injury, barrier disruption, and formation of syncytia in human lung tissue; however, the regulatory host defense mechanisms involved remain poorly defined. ADAM17 is a multifunctional sheddase implicated in inflammatory lung disease and is considered a potential therapeutic target during viral infections. Here, we show that RSV infection induces ADAM17 activity through PKC- and ERK-dependent signaling, increasing surface ADAM17 levels and sheddase activity. Genetic loss or pharmacological inhibition of ADAM17 reduced RSV-induced formation of syncytia, post-entry viral spread, and viral titers. This identifies ADAM17 as a host factor that supports viral dissemination. ADAM17 deficiency simultaneously exacerbated RSV-induced epithelial injury, characterized by loss of intercellular cohesion, impaired barrier function, increased paracellular permeability, and enhanced cytotoxicity. RSV-induced ADAM17 activity promoted the release of multiple epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR) ligands. Supplementation with recombinant amphiregulin partially restored barrier function in infected ADAM17-deficient cells. Consistent with these functional effects, ADAM17 deficiency was associated with the loss of epithelial differentiation-associated transcriptional programs and increased expression of inflammatory genes. These findings indicate that ADAM17 plays a dual role in RSV infection. It facilitates syncytial viral spread, while preserving epithelial integrity through autocrine EGFR signaling. Thus, ADAM17 activity represents a biological trade-off between viral dissemination and tissue protection, indicating that therapeutic ADAM17 inhibition may reduce viral spread at the cost of aggravating epithelial damage. IMPORTANCE During respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, the airway epithelium must maintain barrier integrity while responding to virus-induced syncytium formation and tissue damage. It is poorly understood which host factors balance tissue preservation against viral replication and spread. Here, we demonstrate that the host cellular metalloproteinase ADAM17 is activated upon RSV infection. While RSV-induced ADAM17 activity promotes syncytium formation and viral spread, it concurrently controls the maintenance of epithelial barrier integrity, preserves cell survival, and inhibits hyperinflammatory signaling. By demonstrating that ADAM17 has a dual mode of action controlling both viral propagation and epithelial barrier resilience, this work uncovers a central trade-off: the same host factor exploited by RSV for dissemination is essential for protecting airway tissue. Consequently, targeting ADAM17 for antiviral therapy presents major challenges, as blocking viral spread may compromise vital epithelial defenses.

ADAM17 is a multifunctional sheddase implicated in inflammatory lung disease and is considered a potential therapeutic target during viral infections. Here, we show that RSV infection induces ADAM17 activity through PKC- and ERK-dependent signaling, increasing surface ADAM17 levels and sheddase activity. Genetic loss or pharmacological inhibition of ADAM17 reduced RSV-induced formation of syncytia, post-entry viral spread, and viral titers. This identifies ADAM17 as a host factor that supports viral dissemination. ADAM17 deficiency simultaneously exacerbated RSV-induced epithelial injury, characterized by loss of intercellular cohesion, impaired barrier function, increased paracellular permeability, and enhanced cytotoxicity. RSV-induced ADAM17 activity promoted the release of multiple epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR) ligands. Supplementation with recombinant amphiregulin partially restored barrier function in infected ADAM17-deficient cells. Consistent with these functional effects, ADAM17 deficiency was associated with the loss of epithelial differentiation-associated transcriptional programs and increased expression of inflammatory genes. These findings indicate that ADAM17 plays a dual role in RSV infection. It facilitates syncytial viral spread, while preserving epithelial integrity through autocrine EGFR signaling. Thus, ADAM17 activity represents a biological trade-off between viral dissemination and tissue protection, indicating that therapeutic ADAM17 inhibition may reduce viral spread at the cost of aggravating epithelial damage. IMPORTANCE During respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, the airway epithelium must maintain barrier integrity while responding to virus-induced syncytium formation and tissue damage. It is poorly understood which host factors balance tissue preservation against viral replication and spread. Here, we demonstrate that the host cellular metalloproteinase ADAM17 is activated upon RSV infection. While RSV-induced ADAM17 activity promotes syncytium formation and viral spread, it concurrently controls the maintenance of epithelial barrier integrity, preserves cell survival, and inhibits hyperinflammatory signaling. By demonstrating that ADAM17 has a dual mode of action controlling both viral propagation and epithelial barrier resilience, this work uncovers a central trade-off: the same host factor exploited by RSV for dissemination is essential for protecting airway tissue. Consequently, targeting ADAM17 for antiviral therapy presents major challenges, as blocking viral spread may compromise vital epithelial defenses.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染导致人类肺组织上皮损伤、屏障破坏以及融合体的形成;然而,涉及的调控 宿主 防御机制仍尚未明确。ADAM17 是一种多功能的分离酶,参与炎症性肺病,被视为病毒感染期间的潜在治疗靶点。在此,我们展示 RSV 感染通过 PKC- 和 ERK 依赖性信号激活 ADAM17,提高其表面水平和分离酶活性。遗传性敲除或药物抑制 ADAM17 减少了 RSV 诱导的融合体形成、病毒进入后的传播以及病毒滴度。这表明 ADAM17 是一种 宿主 因子,促进病毒传播。ADAM17 缺失同时加重了 RSV 诱导的上皮损伤,表现为细胞间结合丧失、屏障功能受损、间隙通透性增加以及细胞毒性增强。RSV 诱导的 ADAM17 活性促进了多种上皮生长因子受体 (EGFR) 配体的释放。使用重组表皮生长因子受体配体部分恢复了 ADAM17 缺失细胞的屏障功能。与这些功能效应一致,ADAM17 缺失导致与上皮分化相关的转录程序丧失,并上调炎症基因的表达。这些发现表明 ADAM17 在 RSV 感染中发挥双重作用。它促进融合体病毒传播,同时通过自激素样 EGFR 信号通路保护上皮完整性。因此,ADAM17 活性代表了病毒传播与组织保护之间的生物权衡,表明治疗性 ADAM17 抑制可能降低病毒传播,但会加剧上皮损伤。在 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染期间,气道上皮必须维持屏障完整性,同时应对病毒诱导的融合体形成和组织损伤。目前尚不清楚哪些 宿主 因子在组织保护与病毒复制及传播之间取得平衡。在此,我们展示 宿主 细胞金属蛋白酶 ADAM17 在 RSV 感染时被激活。尽管 RSV 诱导的 ADAM17 活性促进融合体形成和病毒传播,它同时调控上皮屏障完整性的维持、细胞存活的保护以及抑制超炎症信号。通过表明 ADAM17 同时控制病毒传播和上皮屏障韧性,本研究揭示了一个核心权衡:同一被 RSV 利用于传播的 宿主 因子对于保护气道组织至关重要。因此,针对 抗病毒药物 疗法的 ADAM17 靶向面临重大挑战,因为阻断病毒传播可能削弱重要的上皮屏障防护。

papers.title: Safety and Immunogenicity of an mRNA Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine, mRNA-1345, in Healthy and High-Risk Pediatric Populations Aged 2 to 17 Years
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) in infants and children. No active RSV vaccine is currently available for children. mRNA-1345 is an investigational mRNA-based RSV vaccine encoding the prefusion F (preF) glycoprotein. Methods This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind study evaluated a single dose of mRNA-1345 in children aged 2 to 2 years at increased RSV risk, with further evaluation required to characterize the benefit-risk profile in RSV-naïve children.

analysis.summary_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory infections in children, yet no licensed vaccine exists for this population. An abstract reports a phase 2, randomized, observer‐blind trial of mRNA‐1345, an mRNA vaccine encoding the prefusion F glycoprotein, administered as a single dose to children aged two years who are at heightened RSV risk. While the study design and vaccine composition are described, the abstract provides no data on safety, immunogenicity, or efficacy, nor does it include the authors' interpretation, public‐health implications, or discussion of limitations. Consequently, the current evidence is insufficient to assess the vaccine’s performance or its potential impact on RSV prevention strategies.

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The supplied evidence does not report implications for surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, or broader public‐health practice.

papers.title_zh: mRNA 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗、mRNA-1345 在 2 至 17 岁健康和高危儿科人群中的安全性和免疫原性
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) in infants and children. No active RSV vaccine is currently available for children. mRNA-1345 is an investigational mRNA-based RSV vaccine encoding the prefusion F (preF) glycoprotein. Methods This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind study evaluated a single dose of mRNA-1345 in children aged 2 to 2 years at increased RSV risk, with further evaluation required to characterize the benefit-risk profile in RSV-naïve children.
