papers.title: Prospective Cardiac MRI study comparing Recovered COVID-19 patients with Recovered Non-COVID-19 Viral Respiratory Infection Patients (R-COVID-CMR).
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with subclinical myocardial inflammation. Post-COVID-19 infection, there are concerns about subsequent heart failure and persistent myocarditis. It is unknown how COVID-19 infection compares with non-COVID-19 viral infections in terms of myocardial inflammation based on cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) assessment. This prospective longitudinal study aims to determine and compare the extent and severity of myocardial involvement in patients with COVID-19 infection versus non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infections (control). METHOD: Recruited recovered COVID-19 (RCOVID) patients and recovered non-COVID (non-COVID) patients from several hospitals and COVID-19-designated clinic underwent three CMR examinations for functional assessment, native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) quantification, with corroborating blood markers (NT-proBNP, white cell count, c-reactive protein, lactate dehydrogenase, and high sensitivity cardiac troponin T). CMR scans took place (i) within 2-week of confirmed recovery, (ii) 3-month, and (iii) 12-month post-recovery. Linear mixed model with Bonferroni correction was used for analysis. RESULTS: 152 participants were recruited, 112 RCOVID outpatients (mean age: 41.0; 58.9% female) and 40 non-COVID inpatients (mean age:45.0; 37.5% female). Non-COVID infections included influenza virus, rhinovirus/enterovirus, parainfluenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and human metapneumovirus. At all three time points, blood results and cardiac function parameters were not significantly different between RCOVID and non-COVID patient groups (p-value not significant). Both patient groups had no significant differences for native T1/T2 values, ECV, late gadolinium enhancement, T2 short tau inversion recovery, and overall fulfilment of the 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria at each time points. CONCLUSION: In this prospective longitudinal study with CMR examinations, COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse myocardial inflammatory response than non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infection in terms of CMR parameters, and blood markers. PLAIN ENGLISH SUMMARY: During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreaks, some COVID-19 patients were incidentally found to have inflammation of the muscular layer of the heart. Healthcare professionals were concerned the inflammation will lead to heart not delivering enough blood to meet body demands (ie. heart failure) in the long run. Therefore, we designed this study to better understand the extent and severity of cardiac involvement in patients with COVID-19 by comparing them to patients with other types of viral respiratory infections, such as influenza, which we were more familiar with. We recruited two groups of patients, one group with patients recovered from COVID-19, the other group with patients recovered from other types of viral respiratory infections. For each patient, we arranged three assessments at 2 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months after their recovery respectively. During each assessment, they had blood taken and underwent a cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) scan, a type of medical imaging used for assessment of heart function. 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria (LLC) is a set of criteria for diagnosis of myocardial inflammation recommended by a group of experts. We compared the two groups of patients at each time point according to LLC, as well as their blood markers and heart function. In our study, we found that COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse heart muscle inflammatory response than other types of viral respiratory infections. This is reassuring as patients with previous COVID-19 infections will likely not develop inflammation of the heart muscle nor develop heart failure.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to compare the extent and severity of myocardial inflammation in recovered COVID-19 patients with those in recovered non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infection patients using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and blood markers. A total of 152 participants were enrolled, including 112 recovered COVID-19 outpatients and 40 recovered non-COVID-19 inpatients. The study found no significant differences in CMR parameters, blood markers, or cardiac function between the two groups at three time points: 2 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months post-recovery. The results suggest that COVID-19 does not cause a worse myocardial inflammatory response than other viral respiratory infections. The study's findings are relevant for understanding long-term cardiac effects of viral infections and may inform future research and clinical practice. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of reported limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2019 冠状病毒病(COVID-19)与亚临床心肌炎症有关,感染 COVID-19 后,人们担心随后出现心力衰竭和持续性心肌炎。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性纵向研究旨在确定和比较 COVID-19 感染患者与非 COVID-19 病毒性呼吸道感染(对照)患者心肌受累的程度和严重程度。我们招募了两组患者,一组是从 COVID-19 中康复的患者,另一组是从其他类型的病毒性呼吸道感染中康复的患者。
elements_zh.methods: 从多家医院和COVID-19指定诊所招募的康复的COVID-19(RCOVID)患者和康复的非COVID(非COVID)患者接受了三项CMR检查,以进行功能评估、天然T1、T2和细胞外容量(ECV)定量,并进行确证的血液标志物(NT-proBNP、白细胞计数、c反应蛋白、乳酸脱氢酶和高敏心肌肌钙蛋白T)。
elements_zh.main_results: 招募了 152 名参与者,其中 112 名 RCOVID 门诊患者(平均年龄:41.0 岁;58.9% 女性)和 40 名非 COVID 住院患者(平均年龄:45.0 岁;37.5% 女性)。在所有三个时间点,RCOVID 和非 COVID 患者组之间的血液结果和心功能参数没有显着差异(p 值不显着)。两个患者组在每个时间点的天然 T1/T2 值、ECV、晚期钆增强、T2 短 tau 反转恢复以及总体满足 2018 年修订的路易斯湖标准方面没有显着差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项使用 CMR 检查的前瞻性纵向研究中,就 CMR 参数和血液标志物而言,与非 COVID-19 病毒性呼吸道感染相比,COVID-19 感染不会引起更严重的心肌炎症反应。我们根据LLC比较了两组患者在每个时间点的情况,以及他们的血液标志物和心功能。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这令人放心,因为既往感染过 COVID-19 的患者可能不会出现心肌炎症,也不会出现心力衰竭。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据并未报告研究设计的局限性。

papers.title: The role of community pharmacists in updating the vaccination schedule: a descriptive analysis of vaccination data in the greater Paris Region, 2022-2024
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Community pharmacists in France have been authorized to prescribe and administer influenzae vaccines since 2019, and of all vaccines on the immunization schedule for individuals aged 11 years and older in August 2023. A few studies have explored patients’ and pharmacists’ perceptions of vaccination in community pharmacies, but their contribution to vaccination schedule adherence under routine conditions remains limited in France. The aim of this study was to evaluate the implementation of pharmacy-based vaccination in the greater Paris Region (Île-de-France (IDF) region), France. Methods: We analysed the vaccines (excluding COVID-19 vaccines) prescribed and administered by healthcare professionals in the greater Paris Region (Ile de France, IDF) over a three-year period (2022-2024), using the database of the National Health Data System (Système National des Données de Santé, SNDS). Results: The total number of vaccine doses administered by pharmacists in the IDF Region increased from 896,663 in 2022 to 1,802,705 in 2024 (101% increase), mainly due to influenza vaccination (n= 880,845 in 2022 and n= 1,280,744 in 2024). Among vaccines for which recommendations were updated during the study period, the number of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine doses administered in community pharmacies increased from 431 in 2022 to 51,105 in 2024, and 5,089 doses of respiratory syncytial virus vaccine were administered in 2024, compared to none before 2024. In 2024, 67,435 pneumococcal vaccine doses were administered in community pharmacies, of which 2.6% were prescribed by pharmacists. In 2024, 5% of doses (n=27,997/521 961 doses, excluding influenza vaccines) administrated were prescribed by pharmacist. The majority (68%, n= 18,936/27,997) were combined diphtheria-tetanus-poliomyelitis vaccines with reduced-antigen acellular pertussis (dTaP/IPV), while herpes zoster vaccines represented the smallest share (0.1%, n= 41). Of all combined dTaP-IPV vaccines prescribed by pharmacists in 2024 – a year marked by a pertussis epidemic– 95% included the pertussis component. Conclusion: The study evaluates pharmacy-based vaccination activity in the IDF Region, according to prescribing and administration practices. The encouraging rates of prescribing and administration by pharmacists for vaccines with recently updated recommendations highlight pharmacist’s frontline role in infection prevention and their responsiveness to new recommendations and epidemic situations.

analysis.methods: The study used the database of the National Health Data System (SNDS) to analyze vaccines prescribed and administered by healthcare professionals in the greater Paris Region over a three-year period (2022-2024). The study uses data from the National Health Data System (SNDS) and focuses on the implementation of pharmacy-based vaccination. papers.title_zh: 社区药剂师在更新 疫苗接种 时间表中的作用:2022-2024 年大巴黎地区 疫苗接种 数据的描述性分析
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background: Community pharmacists in France have been authorized to prescribe and administer influenzae vaccines since 2019, and of all vaccines on the immunization schedule for individuals aged 11 years and older in August 2023. A few studies have explored patients’ and pharmacists’ perceptions of vaccination in community pharmacies, but their contribution to vaccination schedule adherence under routine conditions remains limited in France. The aim of this study was to evaluate the implementation of pharmacy-based vaccination in the greater Paris Region (Île-de-France (IDF) region), France. Methods: We analysed the vaccines (excluding COVID-19 vaccines) prescribed and administered by healthcare professionals in the greater Paris Region (Ile de France, IDF) over a three-year period (2022-2024), using the database of the National Health Data System (Système National des Données de Santé, SNDS). Results: The total number of vaccine doses administered by pharmacists in the IDF Region increased from 896,663 in 2022 to 1,802,705 in 2024 (101% increase), mainly due to influenza vaccination (n= 880,845 in 2022 and n= 1,280,744 in 2024). Among vaccines for which recommendations were updated during the study period, the number of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine doses administered in community pharmacies increased from 431 in 2022 to 51,105 in 2024, and 5,089 doses of respiratory syncytial virus vaccine were administered in 2024, compared to none before 2024. In 2024, 67,435 pneumococcal vaccine doses were administered in community pharmacies, of which 2.6% were prescribed by pharmacists. In 2024, 5% of doses (n=27,997/521 961 doses, excluding influenza vaccines) administrated were prescribed by pharmacist. The majority (68%, n= 18,936/27,997) were combined diphtheria-tetanus-poliomyelitis vaccines with reduced-antigen acellular pertussis (dTaP/IPV), while herpes zoster vaccines represented the smallest share (0.1%, n= 41). Of all combined dTaP-IPV vaccines prescribed by pharmacists in 2024 – a year marked by a pertussis epidemic– 95% included the pertussis component. Conclusion: The study evaluates pharmacy-based vaccination activity in the IDF Region, according to prescribing and administration practices. The encouraging rates of prescribing and administration by pharmacists for vaccines with recently updated recommendations highlight pharmacist’s frontline role in infection prevention and their responsiveness to new recommendations and epidemic situations.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:自2019年起,法国社区药剂师被授权开具和接种流感疫苗,并且在2023年8月,所有疫苗均被列入11岁及以上个体的免疫接种计划。尽管已有少数研究探讨了患者和药剂师对社区药房疫苗接种的看法,但它们在常规条件下对疫苗接种接种计划依从性的贡献在法国仍然有限。本研究旨在评估法国大巴黎地区(Île-de-France,IDF)社区药房基于药房的疫苗接种实施情况。方法:我们分析了2022年至2024年间,大巴黎地区(Ile de France,IDF)医疗卫生专业人员开具和接种的疫苗(不包括COVID-19 疫苗)的数据,使用国家健康数据系统(Système National des Données de Santé,SNDS)数据库。结果:IDF地区药剂师开具和接种的疫苗剂量总数从2022年的896,663增加到2024年的1,802,705(增长101%),主要由于流感疫苗接种(2022年880,845剂,2024年1,280,744剂)。在研究期间推荐更新的疫苗中,2022年社区药房接种的人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗剂量为431剂,2024年增加到51,105剂,2024年还接种了5,089剂呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗,而此前从未接种过。2024年,社区药房接种了67,435剂肺炎球菌疫苗,其中2.6%由药剂师开具。2024年,5%的接种剂量(27,997/521,961剂,不包括流感疫苗)由药剂师开具。其中,68%(18,936/27,997剂)为结合百日咳-白喉-脊髓灰质炎疫苗,含有减少抗原的无细胞百日咳(dTaP/IPV),而带状疱疹疫苗所占比例最小(0.1%,41剂)。2024年,所有由药剂师开具的结合dTaP-IPV 疫苗中,95%包含百日咳成分。结论:本研究评估了IDF地区基于药房的疫苗接种活动,根据开具和接种实践。对于最近更新推荐的疫苗,药剂师开具和接种的鼓励率突显了他们在感染预防中的前线角色及其对新推荐和疫情情况的响应能力。

papers.title: Public Health Impact of Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccination Among US Adults Aged ≥60 Years Residing in Long-Term Care Settings.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Adults aged ≥60 years and adults with certain health conditions are at increased risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease, which can have a substantial clinical burden. Residents in long-term care settings often have multiple risk factors, including age ≥60 years, underlying health conditions, and/or frailty, compounding risk for severe RSV disease. This study evaluated the public health impact of adjuvanted RSV prefusion F3 (RSVPreF3) vaccination on averted RSV disease burden. DESIGN: Public health impact analysis using a static, multicohort Markov model. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: United States (US) adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings. METHODS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination vs no vaccination was simulated over 5 years using real-world RSV vaccination uptake data. Other model inputs have been previously validated and reported. This analysis estimated avoided RSV-related health outcomes due to vaccination, as well as the number needed to vaccinate (NNV) to avoid RSV-related outcomes. RESULTS: Among the modeled 2,113,600 US adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings, 378,656 were simulated to receive 1 dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3. RSV vaccination resulted in 33,989 fewer RSV cases, including 7688 fewer RSV-upper respiratory tract disease cases and 26,302 fewer RSV-lower respiratory tract disease cases (RSV-LRTD). Avoided healthcare resource use included 19,639 fewer outpatient visits, 1556 fewer emergency department visits, and 11,634 fewer hospitalizations. RSV-related deaths declined by 1355 over 5 years, alongside 7221 and 6043 fewer discounted life years and quality-adjusted life years lost, respectively. To avoid 1 RSV-LRTD case, the estimated NNV was 14 individuals. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination avoided a substantial number of negative health outcomes among US adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings, providing evidence of its impact as a prevention strategy. Future efforts are needed to ensure that long-term care residents have access to RSV vaccination.

source_records.title: Public Health Impact of Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccination Among US Adults Aged ≥60 Years Residing in Long-Term Care Settings.
source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Adults aged ≥60 years and adults with certain health conditions are at increased risk for severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease, which can have a substantial clinical burden. Residents in long-term care settings often have multiple risk factors, including age ≥60 years, underlying health conditions, and/or frailty, compounding risk for severe RSV disease. This study evaluated the public health impact of adjuvanted RSV prefusion F3 (RSVPreF3) vaccination on averted RSV disease burden. DESIGN: Public health impact analysis using a static, multicohort Markov model. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: United States (US) adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings. METHODS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination vs no vaccination was simulated over 5 years using real-world RSV vaccination uptake data. Other model inputs have been previously validated and reported. This analysis estimated avoided RSV-related health outcomes due to vaccination, as well as the number needed to vaccinate (NNV) to avoid RSV-related outcomes. RESULTS: Among the modeled 2,113,600 US adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings, 378,656 were simulated to receive 1 dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3. RSV vaccination resulted in 33,989 fewer RSV cases, including 7688 fewer RSV-upper respiratory tract disease cases and 26,302 fewer RSV-lower respiratory tract disease cases (RSV-LRTD). Avoided healthcare resource use included 19,639 fewer outpatient visits, 1556 fewer emergency department visits, and 11,634 fewer hospitalizations. RSV-related deaths declined by 1355 over 5 years, alongside 7221 and 6043 fewer discounted life years and quality-adjusted life years lost, respectively. To avoid 1 RSV-LRTD case, the estimated NNV was 14 individuals. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccination avoided a substantial number of negative health outcomes among US adults aged ≥60 years residing in long-term care settings, providing evidence of its impact as a prevention strategy. Future efforts are needed to ensure that long-term care residents have access to RSV vaccination.
source_records.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

papers.abstract_zh: OBJECTIVES: ≥60岁成人及具有某些健康状况的成人罹患严重呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疾病的风险增加,这可能带来显著的临床负担。长期护理机构的居民通常具有多种风险因素,包括年龄≥60岁、基础健康状况和/或虚弱,这些因素会增加罹患严重RSV疾病的风险。本研究评估了佐剂RSV PreF3疫苗(RSVPreF3 疫苗接种)对避免RSV疾病负担的公共卫生影响。DESIGN: 使用静态、多队列马尔可夫模型进行公共卫生影响分析。SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: 美国≥60岁居住在长期护理机构的成人。METHODS: 通过使用真实世界RSV 疫苗接种接种数据,模拟了佐剂RSVPreF3 疫苗接种与无接种的对比情况,时间跨度为5年。其他模型输入数据已预先验证并报告。本分析估算了由于接种疫苗接种而避免的RSV相关健康结局,以及避免RSV相关结局所需的疫苗接种人数(NNV)。RESULTS: 在模拟的2,113,600名美国≥60岁长期护理机构居住成人中,有378,656人接种了1剂佐剂RSVPreF3疫苗。RSV 疫苗接种导致了33,989例RSV病例减少,包括7688例RSV上呼吸道疾病病例减少和26,302例RSV下呼吸道疾病病例(RSV-LRTD)减少。避免的医疗资源使用包括19,639例门诊就诊减少、1556例急诊就诊减少和11,634例住院减少。在5年内,RSV相关死亡人数减少了1355例,同时减少了7221和6043例折算生命年和质量调整生命年损失。为避免1例RSV-LRTD病例,估计所需的疫苗接种人数(NNV)为14人。CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: 佐剂RSVPreF3 疫苗接种在美国≥60岁长期护理机构居住成人中避免了大量负面健康结局,提供了其作为预防策略影响的证据。未来需要努力确保长期护理机构居民能够获得RSV 疫苗接种。

papers.title: Size, cytopathic effects, and prevalence of Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV in healthcare settings
papers.abstract: Airborne transmission of respiratory viruses in healthcare settings is difficult to assess, particularly with respect to the size and viability of virus-containing aerosols. Most field studies rely on molecular detection, which limits inference about the infectiousness of virus. In this study we collected size-resolved airborne samples in a dental clinic and hospital during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season using a BC (BioCascade)-BioSpot VIVAS (Viable Virus Aerosol Sampler). We analyzed these samples by RT-PCR and culture-based assays for influenza A, influenza B, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Viral RNA was detected in 11.1% of the 81 sampling events, with the highest positivity (25%) observed in pulmonary unit patient rooms. When influenza and SARS-CoV-2 RNA were detected, all of these detections occurred in the 4-10 μm size fraction, whereas all RSV RNA was detected in the <1.5 μm size fraction. Cell culture assays confirmed the presence of viable influenza in the samples that were positive by RT-PCR. Plaques were only observed for influenza A viral positive samples at the ‘neat’ or undiluted rate, whereas RSV and SARS-CoV-2 did not produce cytopathic effects in the cell culture assays. These findings highlight virus-specific differences in aerosol size distributions and the challenges of recovering viable virus from field-collected bioaerosols in healthcare environments.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess airborne transmission of respiratory viruses in healthcare settings, focusing on the size and viability of virus-containing aerosols. Airborne samples were collected in a dental clinic and hospital during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season using a BC-BioSpot VIVAS sampler. Viral RNA was detected in 11.1% of 81 sampling events, with the highest positivity in pulmonary unit patient rooms. RSV RNA was consistently found in the <1.5 μm size fraction, while influenza and SARS-CoV-2 RNA were detected in the 4-10 μm size fraction. Cell culture assays confirmed the presence of viable influenza in RT-PCR-positive samples, but no cytopathic effects were observed for RSV or SARS-CoV-2. These results emphasize virus-specific differences in aerosol size distributions and the challenges of recovering viable virus from field samples. The study provides insights into the behavior of RSV in healthcare environments but does not address limitations or evidence strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 在医疗保健环境中评估呼吸道病毒气溶胶的传播性(传播)具有挑战性,尤其是在病毒气溶胶的大小和活性方面。大多数现场研究依赖于分子检测,这限制了对病毒传染性的推断。本研究在2024-2025年呼吸道病毒季节期间,使用BC(BioCascade)-BioSpot VIVAS(可培养病毒气溶胶采样器)在牙科诊所和医院中收集了具有粒径分辨率的空气样本。我们通过RT-PCR和基于培养的检测方法分析了这些样本,以检测流感A型、流感B型、SARS-CoV-2和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)。在81次采样事件中,有11.1%的样本检测到病毒RNA,其中肺病单元病房的阳性率最高(25%)。当检测到流感和SARS-CoV-2的RNA时,所有检测均发生在4-10 μm粒径组分中,而所有RSV RNA均检测到在<1.5 μm粒径组分中。细胞培养检测证实了通过RT-PCR检测为阳性的样本中存在可培养的流感病毒。仅在流感A型病毒阳性样本中观察到斑块,而RSV和SARS-CoV-2在细胞培养检测中未产生细胞病变效应。这些发现突显了不同病毒在气溶胶粒径分布上的特异性差异,以及在医疗保健环境中从现场收集的生物气溶胶中回收活性病毒的挑战。

papers.title: Prevalence of respiratory viruses among pilgrims in Saudi Arabia during the Hajj 2026: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hajj is one of the world's largest annual mass gatherings and provides favorable conditions for respiratory virus transmission because of intense crowding and extensive international travel. Contemporary post-pandemic molecular surveillance data remain limited. This study investigated the prevalence, determinants, and characteristics of respiratory virus detections among pilgrims during the 2026 Hajj season. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among adult domestic and international pilgrims over an extended peri-Hajj period (before, during and after Hajj) in the year 2026. Participants completed a structured questionnaire and provided combined nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swab specimens for multiplex real-time RT-PCR detection of common respiratory viruses. A subset of positive samples underwent genomic sequencing for viral subtype and variant characterization. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infection. Results Among 412 enrolled pilgrims across all three phases, 58 (14.1%) tested positive for at least one respiratory virus. The prevalence of viral detection was 6.7% pre-Hajj, 16.0% during Hajj and 21.4% post-Hajj. Influenza A was the predominant virus (34.5%), followed by rhinovirus (24.1%), SARS-CoV-2 (20.7%), respiratory syncytial virus (13.8%), adenovirus (5.2%), and seasonal human coronaviruses (1.7%). Diabetes mellitus, chronic lung disease and smoking were independently associated with increased odds of respiratory virus detection. Conversely, receipt of pre-travel health advice, influenza vaccination and regular facemask use were independently associated with reduced odds of respiratory virus detection. Conclusions Respiratory virus transmission remains an important public health concern during Hajj. Strengthening pre-travel health advice, promoting influenza vaccination, and reinforcing personal preventive measures may reduce respiratory viral transmission during Hajj and other international mass gatherings.

A subset of positive samples underwent genomic sequencing for viral subtype and variant characterization. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infection. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 朝觐是世界上最大的年度大规模聚集活动之一,由于密集的人群和广泛的国际旅行,为呼吸道病毒传播提供了有利条件。疫情后关于呼吸道病毒的分子检测数据仍然有限。本研究调查了2026年朝觐季节期间朝觐者中呼吸道病毒检测的频率、决定因素及特征。方法 在2026年朝觐期间(朝觐前、中、后)进行了一项横断面研究,调查了成人国内和国际朝觐者的健康状况。参与者完成了结构化问卷,并提供了合并的鼻咽和咽拭子样本,用于多重实时逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)检测常见呼吸道病毒。部分阳性样本进行了基因组测序以确定病毒亚型和变种。使用逻辑回归分析确定与实验室确认的呼吸道病毒感染相关的因素。结果 在所有三个阶段共纳入412名朝觐者,其中58名(14.1%)至少检测到一种呼吸道病毒。病毒检测的频率在朝觐前为6.7%,朝觐期间为16.0%,朝觐后为21.4%。流感A型病毒是主要病毒(34.5%),其次是鼻病毒(24.1%)、SARS-CoV-2(20.7%)、呼吸道合胞病毒(13.8%)、腺病毒(5.2%)以及季节性人类冠状病毒(1.7%)。糖尿病、慢性肺病和吸烟与呼吸道病毒检测的高风险独立相关。相反,接受旅行前健康建议、接种流感疫苗和定期佩戴口罩与呼吸道病毒检测的低风险独立相关。结论 呼吸道病毒传播在朝觐期间仍然是重要的公共卫生问题。加强旅行前健康建议、推广流感疫苗接种以及强化个人预防措施可能有助于减少朝觐及其他国际大规模聚集活动中的呼吸道病毒感染。

papers.title: Molecular and Epidemiological Characterization of Seasonal Common Cold Viruses and Host Immune Responses in Symptomatic Patients
papers.abstract: Background: Seasonal respiratory viral infections continue to be a significant public health burden worldwide, accounting for a substantial proportion of outpatient visits, absenteeism, and healthcare expenditures.Human rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for the majority of common cold cases, yet their molecular diversity and host immune interactions complicate prevention and management strategies.Objective: This study aimed to characterize circulating common cold viruses during seasonal outbreaks, evaluate transmission dynamics, investigate viral pathogenicity, and analyze host immune responses in symptomatic patients using molecular diagnostic approaches.Methods: A cross-sectional clinical study was conducted across multiple seasons.Nasopharyngeal samples from patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms were analyzed using RT-PCR and multiplex PCR assays for viral identification.Viral load, pathogenicity markers, and host immune parameters including interferons, cytokines, antibody titers, and T-cell responses were quantified.Epidemiological and environmental variables were correlated with clinical severity.Results: Rhinoviruses represented the predominant viral pathogen, followed by coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and RSV.Viral prevalence peaked during winter months and showed significant associations with ambient temperature and humidity.Elevated viral loads correlated positively with pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNFα) and symptom severity, while stronger adaptive immune responses were associated with improved clinical outcomes.Molecular analyses revealed substantial genetic variability, particularly within rhinovirus capsid proteins, contributing to immune evasion and enhanced transmissibility.Conclusion: Seasonal common cold outbreaks are driven primarily by rhinoviruses exhibiting high replication capacity and genetic diversity.Clinical severity is determined by the interplay between viral load and host immune responses.These findings emphasize the importance of molecular surveillance, optimized diagnostic timing, and immune-modulatory therapeutic strategies to improve patient management in clinical pharmacy practice.
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize circulating common cold viruses during seasonal outbreaks, evaluate transmission dynamics, investigate viral pathogenicity, and analyze host immune responses in symptomatic patients using molecular diagnostic approaches. Seasonal respiratory viral infections continue to be a significant public health burden worldwide, accounting for a substantial proportion of outpatient visits, absenteeism, and healthcare expenditures. Human rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for the majority of common cold cases, yet their molecular diversity and host immune interactions complicate prevention and management strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional clinical study was conducted across multiple seasons. Nasopharyngeal samples from patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms were analyzed using RT-PCR and multiplex PCR assays for viral identification. Viral load, pathogenicity markers, and host immune parameters including interferons, cytokines, antibody titers, and T-cell responses were quantified. Epidemiological and environmental variables were correlated with clinical severity.
analysis.methods: Viral identification was performed using RT-PCR and multiplex PCR assays. Viral load, pathogenicity markers, and host immune parameters were quantified.
analysis.main_results: Rhinoviruses represented the predominant viral pathogen, followed by coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and RSV. Viral prevalence peaked during winter months and showed significant associations with ambient temperature and humidity. Elevated viral loads correlated positively with pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNFα) and symptom severity, while stronger adaptive immune responses were associated with improved clinical outcomes. Molecular analyses revealed substantial genetic variability, particularly within rhinovirus capsid proteins, contributing to immune evasion and enhanced transmissibility.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Seasonal common cold outbreaks are driven primarily by rhinoviruses exhibiting high replication capacity and genetic diversity. Clinical severity is determined by the interplay between viral load and host immune responses. These findings emphasize the importance of molecular surveillance, optimized diagnostic timing, and immune-modulatory therapeutic strategies to improve patient management in clinical pharmacy practice.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for common cold outbreaks. They highlight the need for targeted interventions to manage viral diversity and host immune responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the cross-sectional nature of the study, which precludes establishing causality. Sample size and controls were adequate for the study objectives, but generalizability may be limited. The study provides moderate evidence for the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized circulating common cold viruses during seasonal outbreaks, evaluating transmission dynamics and host immune responses. Rhinoviruses were the predominant pathogen, with genetic variability contributing to immune evasion and transmissibility. Elevated viral loads correlated with symptom severity, emphasizing the importance of molecular surveillance and immune-modulatory strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用分子诊断方法对季节性常见感冒病毒进行表征,评估季节性呼吸道病毒感染的动态变化,调查病毒的致病性,并分析症状患者中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的免疫应答与宿主的免疫相互作用。季节性呼吸道病毒感染仍然是全球重要的公共卫生负担,占门诊就诊、缺勤和医疗支出的相当大比例。人类鼻病毒、冠状病毒、腺病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是大多数感冒病例的主要原因,然而其分子多样性以及与宿主的免疫相互作用使预防和管理策略复杂化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项横断面临床研究在多个季节中进行。对出现急性呼吸道症状的患者的鼻咽样本进行了RT-PCR和多重PCR检测以进行病毒鉴定。定量了病毒载量、致病性标志物以及包括干扰素、细胞因子、抗体滴度和T细胞应答在内的宿主免疫参数。流行病学和环境变量与临床严重程度相关。
elements_zh.methods: 病毒鉴定通过RT-PCR和多重PCR检测进行。病毒载量、致病性标志物以及宿主免疫参数被定量分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 鼻病毒是主要的病毒病原体,其次是冠状病毒、腺病毒和RSV。病毒患病率在冬季达到高峰,并与环境温度和湿度有显著关联。病毒载量升高与促炎细胞因子(IL-6,TNFα)和症状严重程度呈正相关,而更强的适应性免疫应答则与改善的临床结果相关。分子分析显示存在显著的遗传变异,尤其是在鼻病毒衣壳蛋白中,这有助于免疫逃逸和增强传播能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 季节性普通感冒主要由具有高复制能力和遗传多样性的鼻病毒驱动。临床严重程度由病毒载量与宿主和免疫应答之间的相互作用决定。这些发现强调了在临床药学实践中改善患者管理的重要性,包括分子监测、优化的诊断时机以及免疫调节治疗策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为常见感冒的监测、诊断和治疗策略提供信息。它们强调了需要采取针对性干预措施来管理病毒多样性以及宿主和免疫应答。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的设计局限性包括研究的横断面性质,这使得无法建立因果关系。样本量和对照组对于研究目标而言是充足的,但研究结果的可推广性可能受到限制。该研究为研究结果提供了中等程度的证据。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize circulating common cold viruses during seasonal outbreaks, evaluate transmission dynamics, investigate viral pathogenicity, and analyze host immune responses in symptomatic patients using molecular diagnostic approaches. Seasonal respiratory viral infections continue to be a significant public health burden worldwide, accounting for a substantial proportion of outpatient visits, absenteeism, and healthcare expenditures. Human rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for the majority of common cold cases, yet their molecular diversity and host immune interactions complicate prevention and management strategies.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional clinical study was conducted across multiple seasons. Nasopharyngeal samples from patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms were analyzed using RT-PCR and multiplex PCR assays for viral identification. Viral load, pathogenicity markers, and host immune parameters including interferons, cytokines, antibody titers, and T-cell responses were quantified. Epidemiological and environmental variables were correlated with clinical severity.
analysis_en.methods: Viral identification was performed using RT-PCR and multiplex PCR assays. Viral load, pathogenicity markers, and host immune parameters were quantified.
analysis_en.main_results: Rhinoviruses represented the predominant viral pathogen, followed by coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and RSV. Viral prevalence peaked during winter months and showed significant associations with ambient temperature and humidity. Elevated viral loads correlated positively with pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNFα) and symptom severity, while stronger adaptive immune responses were associated with improved clinical outcomes. Molecular analyses revealed substantial genetic variability, particularly within rhinovirus capsid proteins, contributing to immune evasion and enhanced transmissibility.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Seasonal common cold outbreaks are driven primarily by rhinoviruses exhibiting high replication capacity and genetic diversity. Clinical severity is determined by the interplay between viral load and host immune responses. These findings emphasize the importance of molecular surveillance, optimized diagnostic timing, and immune-modulatory therapeutic strategies to improve patient management in clinical pharmacy practice.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for common cold outbreaks. They highlight the need for targeted interventions to manage viral diversity and host immune responses.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the cross-sectional nature of the study, which precludes establishing causality. Sample size and controls were adequate for the study objectives, but generalizability may be limited. The study provides moderate evidence for the findings.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:季节性呼吸道病毒感染仍然是全球重要的公共卫生负担,占门诊就诊、缺勤和医疗支出的相当大比例。人类鼻病毒、冠状病毒、腺病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是普通感冒病例的主要原因,但它们的分子多样性以及抗病毒药物免疫相互作用使预防和管理策略复杂化。目标:本研究旨在利用分子诊断方法,描述季节性呼吸道病毒感染期间流行的普通感冒病毒,评估抗病毒药物动力学,研究病毒致病性,并分析症状患者中的免疫参数。方法:在多个季节中进行了一项横断面临床研究。通过RT-PCR和多重PCR检测鼻咽样本中的病毒,以识别病毒。量化了病毒载量、致病性标志物以及抗病毒药物相关的免疫参数,包括干扰素、细胞因子、抗体滴度和T细胞反应。流行病学和环境变量与临床严重程度相关联。结果:鼻病毒是主要的病毒病原体,其次是冠状病毒、腺病毒和RSV。病毒载量在冬季达到峰值,并与环境温度和湿度显著相关。病毒载量升高与促炎细胞因子(IL-6、TNFα)和症状严重程度呈正相关,而更强的适应性免疫反应则与改善的临床结果相关。分子分析显示存在显著的遗传变异,尤其是在鼻病毒衣壳蛋白中,这有助于免疫逃逸和增强传播能力。结论:季节性普通感冒主要由具有高复制能力和遗传多样性的鼻病毒驱动。临床严重程度由病毒载量与免疫反应之间的相互作用决定。这些发现强调了在临床药学实践中,分子监测、优化诊断时机以及免疫调节治疗策略的重要性,以改善患者管理。

papers.title: Host-Dependent Mechanisms of Secondary Bacterial Pneumonia After Viral Infection: Insights from MHV, SARS-CoV-2, and Pulmonary Macrophages
papers.abstract: Respiratory viral infections are a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, partly because they increase susceptibility to secondary bacterial pneumonia and sepsis. Coronaviruses, influenza viruses, parainfluenza viruses, rhinoviruses, and respiratory syncytial virus have each been associated with impaired macrophage antibacterial function, although the underlying evidence differs among virus families. Direct lysosomal-pH measurements and mechanistically resolved links between infection and lysosomal de-acidification are strongest for coronaviruses. Using β-coronaviruses as the primary model for the effect of direct lysosomal disruption on macrophage antimicrobial capacity, this review examines lysosomal exploitation during viral egress, impaired phagosome-lysosome fusion, E-protein-mediated proton conductance, and ORF3a-associated lysosomal injury. It further proposes that the magnitude of these effects is shaped by host-dependent immunometabolic processes. Mitochondrial dysfunction, NAD+ depletion, and disrupted mitochondria-lysosome coupling may reduce the ability of macrophages to preserve lysosomal acidity, autophagic competence, and bacterial killing during viral challenge. Together, these mechanisms describe how coronavirus infection compromises macrophage antibacterial defense, and how the resulting susceptibility to secondary bacterial infection is further modulated by the metabolic and inflammatory state of the host cell.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on host-dependent mechanisms of secondary bacterial pneumonia following viral infection, specifically examining how respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) affects macrophage antibacterial function. It explores the role of lysosomal de-acidification, viral egress, phagosome-lysosome fusion, E-protein-mediated proton conductance, and ORF3a-associated lysosomal injury in this context.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a preprint that analyzes the impact of respiratory syncytial virus on macrophage function through a narrative synthesis of existing literature. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods, but instead provides a general overview of the mechanisms involved.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that respiratory syncytial virus infection impairs macrophage antibacterial defense through lysosomal de-acidification and disrupted immunometabolic processes. It highlights the role of viral proteins in modulating lysosomal function and the host's metabolic state in shaping the magnitude of these effects.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while multiple viruses are associated with impaired macrophage function, the evidence for respiratory syncytial virus is more direct and mechanistically resolved. However, the exact mechanisms of lysosomal disruption and their full impact on bacterial susceptibility remain areas of limited understanding.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on understanding the host-dependent immunometabolic processes that influence the severity of secondary bacterial pneumonia following RSV infection. It also highlights the need for targeted interventions to preserve macrophage function during viral challenges.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection impairs macrophage antibacterial function, leading to increased susceptibility to secondary bacterial pneumonia. It identifies key mechanisms such as lysosomal de-acidification, viral egress, and E-protein-mediated proton conductance, while emphasizing the role of host-dependent immunometabolic processes in modulating these effects. The review highlights the need for further research into the host-virus interactions that influence bacterial susceptibility and suggests potential areas for targeted interventions to improve outcomes in RSV-infected individuals.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于病毒感染后继发性细菌性肺炎中宿主依赖的机制,具体探讨呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)如何影响巨噬细胞的抗菌功能。它分析了溶酶体去酸化、病毒出芽、吞噬体-溶酶体融合、E蛋白介导的质子传导以及ORF3a相关溶酶体损伤在这一背景下的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是一篇预印本,通过现有文献的叙述性综合分析,探讨呼吸道合胞病毒对巨噬细胞功能的影响。它并未报告特定数据库、检索日期或元分析方法,而是提供了一般性的机制概述。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,呼吸道合胞病毒感染通过溶酶体去酸化和免疫代谢过程的破坏,削弱了巨噬细胞的抗菌防御能力。它强调了病毒蛋白在调节溶酶体功能中的作用,以及宿主的代谢状态在塑造这些效应强度中的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,尽管多种病毒与巨噬细胞功能受损有关,但呼吸道合胞病毒的相关证据更为直接且机制明确。然而,溶酶体破坏的确切机制及其对细菌易感性的全部影响仍存在有限的理解。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议未来的研究应关注理解依赖宿主的免疫代谢过程,这些过程会影响呼吸道合胞病毒感染后继发性细菌性肺炎的严重程度。它还强调了在病毒挑战期间有针对性地干预以维持巨噬细胞功能的必要性。

Mitochondrial dysfunction, NAD+ depletion, and disrupted mitochondria-lysosome coupling may reduce the ability of macrophages to preserve lysosomal acidity, autophagic competence, and bacterial killing during viral challenge. Together, these mechanisms describe how coronavirus infection compromises macrophage antibacterial defense, and how the resulting susceptibility to secondary bacterial infection is further modulated by the metabolic and inflammatory state of the host cell.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染是全球发病率和死亡率的重要原因,部分原因是它们会增加继发性细菌性肺炎和败血症的易感性。冠状病毒、流感病毒、副流感病毒、鼻病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒均与巨噬细胞抗菌功能受损有关,尽管不同病毒家族的潜在证据存在差异。对于冠状病毒而言,直接溶酶体pH值的测量以及感染与溶酶体去酸化之间的机制性联系最为明确。本综述以β冠状病毒为主要模型,探讨直接溶酶体破坏对巨噬细胞抗菌能力的影响,具体分析了病毒出芽过程中溶酶体的利用、吞噬体-溶酶体融合受损、E蛋白介导的质子传导以及ORF3a相关溶酶体损伤。此外,综述还提出这些效应的强度可能受到宿主依赖的免疫代谢过程的影响。线粒体功能障碍、NAD+耗竭以及线粒体-溶酶体耦合的破坏可能会降低巨噬细胞在病毒感染期间维持溶酶体酸性、自噬能力和细菌杀灭能力的能力。综上所述,这些机制描述了冠状病毒感染如何削弱巨噬细胞的抗菌防御能力,以及这种继发性细菌感染易感性如何进一步受到宿主细胞代谢和炎症状态的影响。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于病毒感染后继发性细菌性肺炎中宿主依赖的机制,具体探讨呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)如何影响巨噬细胞的抗菌功能。它分析了溶酶体去酸化、病毒出芽、吞噬体-溶酶体融合、E蛋白介导的质子传导以及ORF3a相关溶酶体损伤在这一背景下的作用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是一篇预印本,通过现有文献的叙述性综合分析,探讨呼吸道合胞病毒对巨噬细胞功能的影响。它并未报告特定数据库、检索日期或元分析方法,而是提供了一般性的机制概述。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,呼吸道合胞病毒感染通过溶酶体去酸化和免疫代谢过程的破坏,削弱了巨噬细胞的抗菌防御能力。它强调了病毒蛋白在调节溶酶体功能中的作用,以及宿主的代谢状态在塑造这些效应强度中的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,尽管多种病毒与巨噬细胞功能受损有关,但呼吸道合胞病毒的相关证据更为直接且机制明确。然而,溶酶体破坏的确切机制及其对细菌易感性的全部影响仍存在有限的理解。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议未来的研究应关注理解依赖宿主的免疫代谢过程,这些过程会影响呼吸道合胞病毒感染后继发性细菌性肺炎的严重程度。它还强调了在病毒挑战期间有针对性地干预以维持巨噬细胞功能的必要性。

papers.title: Immune Imprinting Across Respiratory Virus Infection, Vaccination, and Passive Immunization: Rethinking ‘Original Antigenic Sin’ in Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV
papers.abstract: Immune imprinting shapes every subsequent response to antigenically related pathogens and is now central to designing updated vaccines for influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The label “Original Antigenic Sin” has framed imprinting as a fixed liability, but recent germinal-center, B-cell repertoire, and epidemiological data show that the effect is neither uniformly harmful nor irreversible. This review distinguishes cross-reactive immune memory from immune imprinting, defined here as a preferential bias toward the first-encountered antigen. Prior exposure can provide useful cross-reactive memory, but available evidence generally does not show that first-antigen bias itself improves protection relative to an equivalent unbiased memory response. We therefore use a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to examine how antigenic distance, conserved-epitope accessibility, and exposure interval may influence both the usefulness of recalled memory and the extent to which imprinting restricts recruitment of responses to later antigens. The framework organizes existing observations and is not intended to predict imprinting outcomes ex ante. We discuss recent quantitative models that explicitly formalize competition between memory and de novo responses as complementary, pathogen-specific approaches. Across influenza and SARS-CoV-2, early exposure can establish cross-reactive memory associated with subsequent heterologous protection, while preferential recall of the priming antigen may limit responses to novel epitopes. For RSV, the effects of maternal vaccination and passive antibodies on subsequent active immune memory remain uncertain. Immunogen engineering, schedule adjustment, adjuvant selection, and cohort-tailored strategies may broaden pre-existing memory toward conserved protective epitopes and reduce restrictive first-antigen bias.

papers.abstract_zh: 免疫印记塑造了对表型相关病原体的每一次后续免疫应答,并且现在是设计更新版疫苗(流感、SARS-CoV-2和呼吸道合胞病毒,即呼吸道合胞病毒)的核心。‘原始抗原罪’这一标签将免疫印记视为一种固定的不利因素,但近期的生发中心、B细胞谱系和流行病学数据表明,这种效应既不是普遍有害的,也不是不可逆的。本综述区分了交叉反应性免疫记忆与免疫印记,后者被定义为对首次接触抗原的偏好性偏向。先前暴露可以提供有用的交叉反应性记忆,但现有证据通常并未显示首次抗原偏向本身相较于等效的无偏记忆应答能提供更好的保护效果。因此,我们采用一个假设生成的概念框架,探讨抗原距离、保守抗原表位的可接近性以及暴露间隔如何影响回忆性记忆的有用性以及免疫印记对后续抗原反应招募的限制程度。该框架旨在组织现有观察结果,而不是预测免疫印记的先验结果。我们讨论了近期的定量模型,这些模型明确地将记忆反应与新发反应之间的竞争视为互补的、病原体特异性的方法。在流感和SARS-CoV-2中,早期暴露可以建立与后续异源保护相关的交叉反应性记忆,而对初始抗原的偏好性回忆可能会限制对新抗原表位的反应。对于RSV,母体疫苗接种和被动抗体对后续主动免疫记忆的影响仍不确定。免疫原工程、接种时间调整、佐剂选择以及针对队列研究的策略可能会扩大已有的记忆反应,使其朝向保守的保护性抗原表位,并减少对初始抗原的限制性偏向。

papers.title: Effects of vaccination programmes on antibiotic consumption and antimicrobial resistance: a global scoping review
papers.abstract: Vaccination can reduce antimicrobial resistance (AMR) by preventing infections that trigger antibiotic treatment, lowering transmission of resistant vaccine-targeted strains and reducing population antibiotic selection pressure. This scoping review mapped global primary evidence published from 1999 to 2025 on vaccination, antibiotic use and microbiological resistance. The review followed Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance and was reported using PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S. PubMed was searched in June 2026 for records published from 1999 to 2025; Europe PMC, WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar and backward/forward citation searching were retained as supplementary discovery and verification routes. Comparative human primary studies were eligible when vaccination was linked to antibiotic prescribing, dispensing or consumption, or to phenotypic or genotypic resistance. A prespecified term-based prioritization step was followed by detailed title/abstract and full-record assessment. One reviewer conducted initial screening and a second author verified all inclusions and full-record exclusions. Data were charted by vaccine, population, design, outcome and effect estimate, and design-appropriate JBI domains informed interpretation. The PubMed strategy returned 7,433 records; nine additional PubMed-indexed studies were identified through citation chaining. Seventy-four primary studies were included: 35 addressed antibiotic use and 39 direct resistance-related outcomes. Influenza vaccination generally reduced respiratory antibiotic exposure, although null trials and seasonal heterogeneity prevented a universal effect. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines produced modest reductions in all-cause use, larger syndrome-specific reductions and marked declines in resistant vaccine-type disease. Quantitative examples included 8% vaccine effectiveness against outpatient antimicrobial purchases, a 14.7% indirect reduction in otitis-related antimicrobial purchases and declines in nonsusceptible invasive pneumococcal disease from 43.9 to 3.2 per 100,000 children aged < 5 years in long-term US surveillance. An investigational maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccine reduced infant antimicrobial prescribing by 12.9%; rotavirus, COVID-19 and typhoid studies extended the pathway beyond influenza and pneumococcus. Serotype replacement and ecological confounding limited inference for total AMR burden. Vaccination is an upstream component of antimicrobial stewardship, with the strongest evidence for reduced influenza-associated prescribing and resistant vaccine-type pneumococcal disease. Vaccine programmes should be integrated with diagnostic and prescribing stewardship and sustained serotype, genomic and antimicrobial-consumption surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates the impact of vaccination programmes on antibiotic consumption and antimicrobial resistance, focusing on human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and related entities. The review mapped global primary evidence published from 1999 to 2025, using PubMed and supplementary sources. It found that vaccination can reduce AMR by preventing infections that require antibiotic treatment, lowering transmission of resistant strains, and reducing population antibiotic selection pressure. The strongest evidence was for reduced influenza-associated prescribing and resistant vaccine-type pneumococcal disease. However, controversies include seasonal heterogeneity and ecological confounding. Research and practice implications suggest integrating vaccination with antimicrobial stewardship and maintaining surveillance of serotype, genomic, and antimicrobial-consumption data.

papers.abstract_zh: 疫苗接种可以减少抗生素抗性(AMR)的发生,通过预防触发抗生素使用治疗的感染,降低针对疫苗的耐药菌株的发病率,并减少抗生素的选择压力。本综述性研究从1999年至2025年全球主要证据进行了映射,遵循了Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI)的指导,并使用了PRISMA-ScR和PRISMA-S进行报告。2026年6月,PubMed检索了1999年至2025年的记录;欧洲PMC、WHO全球医学索引、Google Scholar和引文追溯作为补充发现和验证途径保留。当疫苗接种与抗生素处方、分发或消耗,或与表型或基因型耐药性相关时,符合条件的人类主要研究比较。按照预设的基于术语的优先级步骤,随后进行了详细的标题/摘要和全文评估。一名审查员进行了初步筛选,第二位作者验证了所有纳入和排除的全文。数据按疫苗、人群、设计、结果和效应估计以及适当的设计领域进行记录,以指导解释。PubMed策略返回了7,433篇记录;通过引文链识别了9项额外的PubMed索引研究。共纳入74项主要研究:35项研究了抗生素使用情况,39项直接研究了耐药相关结果。流感疫苗接种通常减少了呼吸道抗生素暴露,尽管无效应试验和季节性异质性阻碍了普遍效应的确定。肺炎球菌结合疫苗产生了适度的抗生素总体使用减少,特定综合征的更大减少以及耐药疫苗型疾病的显著下降。定量示例包括8%的疫苗对门诊抗菌药物购买的效力,14.7%的中耳炎相关抗菌药物购买的间接减少,以及在5岁以下儿童中非敏感侵袭性肺炎球菌病从每100,000人43.9例下降到3.2例的长期美国监测。一项正在进行的母体呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗减少了婴儿抗菌药物处方12.9%;轮状病毒、COVID-19和伤寒研究将途径扩展到流感和肺炎球菌之外。血清型替代和生态混杂限制了对总体AMR负担的推断。疫苗接种是抗菌管理的上游组成部分,具有减少流感相关处方和耐药疫苗型肺炎球菌疾病的最佳证据。疫苗项目应与诊断和处方管理相结合,并持续进行血清型、基因组和抗菌药物消耗的监测监测。

papers.title: Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0-14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with mortality and DALY rates having declined by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The COVID-19 pandemic drove burden to a historic low in 2021, but a marked rebound followed in 2022-2023, though rates remained below pre-pandemic levels. Infants aged <1 year bore the heaviest burden (mortality 8.688 per 100,000), and India ranked highest, whereas Australia ranked lowest. Burden strongly correlated inversely with Sociodemographic Index. These findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members.

papers.title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV —Important Lessons Learned
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime—oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Methods Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock‐vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. Results We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV‐vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV‐specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. Conclusion Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi‐center preclinical vaccine studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime—oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in a dual-center, randomized, blinded primate model. supplementary_news.content: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS TIMES au NEWSLETTER SIGNUP My account Log Out Oct 21, 9:59 AM AEDT Business News Sports Technology Entertainment Health NEWSLETTER My account Log Out Australia edition Business News Sports Technology Entertainment Health Editions Australia India International Singapore United Kingdom United States NEWSLETTER Follow Us Editions Australia India International Singapore United Kingdom United States Health Healthy Living 10 Ways Seniors Can Keep Their Lungs Healthy and Breathe Easier as Respiratory Virus Season Gets Underway Vaccination, physical activity, cleaner air and managing chronic conditions can help reduce respiratory risks as flu, COVID-19 and RSV spread more widely. By Jerry Thompson Published 10/20/26 AT 4:11 PM AEDT Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket 10 Ways Seniors Can Keep Their Lungs Healthy and Breathe Easier as Respiratory Virus Season Gets Underway As fall turns to winter, respiratory viruses such as flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, begin to spread more widely. For older adults, these infections can be especially dangerous, leading to pneumonia, hospitalization and, in some cases, death. Lung function naturally declines with age. The muscles that help with breathing can weaken, the lungs become less elastic, and the immune system may not respond as strongly to infections. Chronic conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD, asthma and heart disease can add to the risk. But health experts say there is a lot older adults can do to protect their lungs. Here are 10 tips to help seniors keep their lungs healthy. 1. Stay up to date on vaccines Vaccination is one of the most effective ways to protect against serious respiratory illness. Health officials recommend that older adults talk with their health care providers about flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal and RSV vaccines. RSV is a particular concern. The virus leads to as many as 180,000 hospitalizations a year among adults 50 and older, according to the American Lung Association. "During the 2025-26 season, RSV contributed to as many as 25,000 deaths across all ages," Harold Wimmer, president and CEO of the American Lung Association, said this month as the group launched a campaign urging older adults to discuss vaccination with their providers. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends a single dose of RSV vaccine for adults 75 and older and for adults 50 to 74 who are at increased risk of severe illness. Unlike the flu shot, the RSV vaccine is not given every year. Yet as of February, only 43% of adults 75 and older reported ever receiving one, according to the Lung Association. 2. Don't smoke, and avoid secondhand smoke Smoking remains the leading cause of lung disease, including lung cancer and COPD. Quitting at any age can improve lung health and reduce the risk of serious illness. Older adults who smoke can get help from their doctor, local quit programs or the national quitline at 1-800-QUIT-NOW. Avoiding secondhand smoke is also important, as it can irritate the lungs and worsen existing conditions. 3. Stay physically active Regular exercise strengthens the heart and the muscles used for breathing, helping the lungs work more efficiently. Walking, swimming, cycling and tai chi are good low-impact options for older adults. Federal guidelines recommend that older adults aim for about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, adjusted to their abilities. People with lung conditions should check with their doctor before starting a new routine. Some may benefit from pulmonary rehabilitation, a supervised program that combines exercise and education. 4. Practice breathing exercises Breathing techniques can help strengthen the diaphragm and improve breathing efficiency. Two commonly recommended exercises are pursed-lip breathing, which involves breathing in through the nose and out slowly through pursed lips, and diaphragmatic, or belly, breathing. These exercises can be especially helpful for people with COPD or other conditions that cause shortness of breath. 5. Protect yourself from air pollution Outdoor air pollution and wildfire smoke can irritate the lungs and trigger breathing problems. Older adults should check local air quality reports and limit time outdoors when pollution levels are high. On poor air quality days, staying indoors with windows closed and using an air purifier with a HEPA filter can help reduce exposure. 6. Keep indoor air clean Indoor air quality matters too. Dust, mold, pet dander, cleaning chemicals and fumes from gas stoves can affect breathing. Experts recommend keeping homes well ventilated, cleaning regularly to reduce dust and mold, and using cleaning products with fewer harsh chemicals. Homeowners should also test for radon, a naturally occurring radioactive gas that is a leading cause of lung cancer. Test kits are widely available at hardware stores. 7. Wash your hands and avoid germs Simple steps can reduce the spread of respiratory infections. Washing hands frequently with soap and water, avoiding close contact with people who are sick and staying home when ill can help prevent illness. During periods of high virus activity, some older adults choose to wear masks in crowded indoor settings for extra protection. 8. Manage chronic conditions People living with asthma, COPD, heart disease or diabetes should work closely with their health care team to keep those conditions under control. Well-managed conditions can help the lungs better withstand and recover from infections. That includes taking medications as prescribed, using inhalers correctly and following an action plan for flare-ups. 9. Ask about lung cancer screening Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in the United States, but early detection can improve outcomes. Federal guidelines recommend annual low-dose CT screening for adults ages 50 to 80 who have a significant smoking history and currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years. Older adults should ask their doctor whether screening is right for them. 10. Know the warning signs Recognizing symptoms early can help prevent serious complications. Older adults should seek medical care for persistent coughing, shortness of breath, wheezing, chest pain, fever, or coughing up blood. Infections such as RSV and flu can quickly lead to pneumonia in older adults. Early treatment, including antiviral medications for some infections, can make a significant difference. The bottom line While some decline in lung function is a natural part of aging, healthy habits can make a meaningful difference. Staying active, avoiding smoke and pollution, keeping vaccinations current and managing chronic conditions can help older adults breathe easier and stay healthier through respiratory virus season and beyond. As always, older adults should talk with their doctor about their individual health needs, especially before making major changes to their routine or if they have existing medical conditions. © Copyright 2026 IBTimes AU. supplementary_news.content: メインコンテンツへスキップ Towards a future where we can reduce the 'anxiety' of RSV. Preventive measures to protect babies are spreading | Autumn 2026 小児医療アドバイザー 2026年10月15日 16:31 "Huh? This is clearly mild." That is what I felt recently when I saw two cases of babies under 3 months old who were infected with RSV. RSV infection in tiny babies keeps us pediatric staff on high alert. Will their breathing become difficult? Are they able to drink milk? Can they get through this without being hospitalized? It is precisely because we have been watching over them in that way that this recent impression has stayed with me. Of course, this is my personal clinical observation. One cannot judge the effectiveness of prevention based on a small number of cases. Even so, I feel hopeful about the progress in preventive measures to protect babies now. To be able to protect babies even before they are born In April 2026, the RSV vaccine for pregnant women, 'Abrysvo,' became a routine vaccination. The 'antibodies' produced in the mother's body pass through the placenta to the baby. Those antibodies protect the baby after birth from pneumonia, bronchiolitis, and other conditions caused by RSV. Being able to deliver protective power in advance to a tiny baby who has just been born. Don't you think this is a welcome change? There are also preventive methods that deliver antibodies directly to the baby after birth. Which method is suitable is discussed with a doctor based on the mother's vaccination history and the baby's condition. Note that the latest national vaccination rate for the autumn of 2026 could not be confirmed. I cannot tell you at this time what percentage of pregnant women are being vaccinated. I am paying attention to how RSV infections and the severity of cases in babies will change in the first year that this prevention has spread. "I hope the moments that cause anxiety will decrease, even if only a little." There was a case of a 10-month-old who received RSV prevention at their own expense and did not develop a fever. However, not having a fever does not prove the effectiveness of the prevention or that the case is 'mild'. What we should look at is the child's condition, including their breathing, how they are drinking, and their overall energy. While cherishing that, I hope that from now on, there will be even a little less anxiety about RSV! That is what I am hoping for. For babies to be able to spend their time more comfortably. For families to have more time to watch over them with peace of mind. I hope that progress in prevention will lead to such days. What I want to protect is their breathing now, and their breathing in the future. Here, let me share one thing I learned as a Pediatric Allergy Educator. There is a term called 'airway remodeling'. The airway is the passage for air to enter and leave the lungs. In asthma, persistent inflammation can cause the airway walls to thicken and change their structure, making it difficult for the airway to return to its original state of easy airflow. This is called airway remodeling. That is why it is important to watch over children who have repeated coughing or wheezing, connect them to appropriate treatment, and maintain a good condition. Care that reduces the 'distress' of today also leads to supporting their breathing in the future. I would like to share this perspective with those who are involved with children. It should be noted that whether RSV prevention can also prevent future asthma still requires research. Having had RSV once does not mean that a child's future is determined. When you learn, you can notice more things in your daily childcare. For example, a baby who has no fever but is not drinking as much milk as usual. Instead of just thinking, 'They don't have a fever, so they must be fine,' you gain more points to look at, such as: 'How is their breathing?' 'Is their chest sinking in every time they breathe?' 'Do they have their usual energy?' and so on. And the words we use to communicate with parents will also change. “Today, they have only been able to drink about half of what they usually do.” “They don't have a fever, but I am concerned about their breathing.” Learn. Notice. Communicate specifically. Connect to necessary medical care. Each of these actions becomes a way to protect the child. When breathing seems difficult or the child cannot drink, ensure they are taken to a medical institution regardless of whether they have a fever. Turning 'I'm glad I knew that' into peace of mind for children Because you spend every day by their side, there are small changes you can notice. When knowledge is added to that, how you watch over them and how you communicate becomes much more specific. What we want to foster through the Pediatric Medical Advisor training is exactly that kind of 'knowledge that can be used for the sake of children.' Engaging with them while looking ahead not only to their current physical condition but also to their healthy growth in the future. Let's work together to cultivate the power to protect children. Pediatric Medical Advisor HOIKU to CARE *Information regarding systems and research is current as of October 15, 2026. Case descriptions are based on individual clinical experience. Conditions Winter Hospital Peaks From COVID-19, Flu and RSV Expected Near Last Season's Level as Early Flu Activity Climbs Published Oct 19, 2026 7:45 AM EDT By Cole Mercer Tim Boyle | Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket U.S. hospitals should plan for a winter respiratory peak about as heavy as last season's, according to the CDC's outlook for the 2026–2027 season, which the agency's October 16 respiratory illness update continues to point to. The CDC expects the combined peak in hospitalizations from COVID-19, flu, and RSV to be within 20% of last season's peak, with low to moderate confidence. The update arrives as flu activity runs ahead of the usual calendar. In the week ending October 10, 5.0% of clinical lab specimens tested positive for influenza, up from 3.9% the week before, according to the CDC's FluView report, with the highest activity on the West Coast. National activity remains low overall. For households, a season like last year's still means crowded emergency rooms, missed work and school, and real danger for babies, older adults and people with chronic illness. The CDC says the outlook offers high-level information on how the season could unfold and stresses that "it is not a forecast." Putting "Similar to Last Season" Into Numbers Last season's combined peak came in the week ending January 3, 2026, according to the CDC. This year's CDC season outlook for COVID-19, flu, and RSV, published September 23, lays out what a similar season could look like for each virus. For COVID-19, modeling suggests a peak weekly hospitalization rate of 1.4 to 2.5 per 100,000 people in early to mid-January if no new immune-evading variant appears. If a variant with moderate immune escape emerges, the projected peak rises to 2.8 to 6.7 per 100,000, likely in late January 2027. About two-thirds of the experts the CDC surveyed considered that scenario unlikely. For flu, the CDC expects a moderate season across all ages, with low to moderate confidence. Last season was moderate overall but high in severity for children. For RSV, the CDC expects a peak within 20% of last season's, with moderate confidence. RSV peaked unusually late last season, in the week ending February 21, 2026, and the CDC says that may signal another late peak this season. Timing is hard to predict. COVID-19 hospitalizations usually peak in late December or early January, flu between December and February, and RSV around late December or early January. When those peaks overlap, hospitals feel the combined strain. The CDC lists several reasons the peak could run higher: a new COVID-19 variant, flu mutations that weaken immune protection, more severe strains, and lower vaccine uptake or effectiveness than last season. West Coast Flu Climbs Ahead of the Usual Calendar FluView shows activity highest in HHS Regions 9 and 10, which include California, Arizona, Nevada, Hawaii, Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Alaska. The CDC called early-season activity higher than typical for this time of year but within expected seasonal variation. Nationally, 2.1% of outpatient visits were for flu-like illness, below the 2.9% baseline. Hospitals reported 4,024 lab-confirmed flu admissions that week, a rate of 1.2 per 100,000 people, with adults 65 and older highest at 3.8 per 100,000. No flu-related pediatric deaths had been reported for the new season, and no new human infections with novel flu viruses were reported as of October 14. Most flu viruses identified so far are A(H1N1). Early lab testing found that 94.6% of characterized H1N1 viruses, and all tested H3N2 and B/Victoria viruses, were well recognized by antibodies against this season's vaccine strains. That is an encouraging early signal, but it does not guarantee how well the vaccine will work. Elsewhere, the CDC's October 16 update said COVID-19 activity remains elevated in some regions but is declining nationally, RSV activity is very low, and rhinovirus and enterovirus, common causes of colds, are elevated. Protecting Babies, Older Parents, and Chronically Ill Relatives The CDC recommends annual flu vaccination for everyone 6 months and older, ideally in September or October. Flu vaccines prevented an estimated 180,000 hospitalizations in the 2024-2025 season, according to the outlook. For RSV, CDC's RSV vaccine recommendations call for vaccinating adults 75 and older and adults 50 to 74 who are at increased risk. Infants under 8 months can be protected through maternal vaccination during pregnancy or a long-acting antibody shot. Adults considering a 2026–2027 COVID-19 vaccine can ask a doctor or pharmacist whether it fits their age and health and how their plan covers it. Prescription flu antivirals work best when started early and matter most for higher-risk patients, the CDC says. People with fever, cough or shortness of breath should rest, stay hydrated and seek care for severe symptoms such as difficulty breathing, chest pain, confusion or bluish lips. Families with an infant, an older parent or someone with a chronic condition at home may want a plan now for testing, telehealth visits and where to go after hours. Parents of young children can also ask their pediatrician whether the office offers same-day sick visits or a nurse line during peak months. The CDC says it will update the outlook if any virus shifts course, and it posts new respiratory data every Friday. For now, the agency's outlook suggests this winter will likely look familiar, and the steps that helped last season still apply. The CDC expects the combined peak in COVID-19, flu, and RSV hospitalizations to be within 20% of last season's peak, with low to moderate confidence. When will respiratory illness peak? COVID-19 and RSV usually peak in late December or early January, and flu between December and February. RSV peaked late last season and could do so again. Is flu already spreading? Yes, but activity remains low nationally. Flu test positivity rose to 5.0% in the week ending October 10, with the highest activity in West Coast states. What could make the season worse? A new COVID-19 variant, flu mutations that weaken immune protection, more severe strains, or lower vaccine uptake or effectiveness could push the peak higher than expected. Who faces the highest risk? Young children, adults 65 and older, pregnant people, and those with chronic conditions or weakened immune systems face the greatest risk of severe illness. How can families prepare? Get recommended flu, RSV, and COVID-19 shots after talking with a clinician, know when to seek care, and ask early about antivirals for high-risk relatives who get sick. Older age increased the odds of mechanical ventilation, which was strongly associated with mortality. Nearly half of patients with paired lung function tests experienced an FEV1 decline exceeding 10%. RSV IN lung transplant recipients was associated with respiratory failure, declining lung function, and mortality in hospitalized patients. An international multicenter study of 155 adult lung transplant recipients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection identified clinical predictors of severe complications, highlighting the importance of early assessment and continued monitoring in this vulnerable population. RSV in Lung Transplant Recipients: Severe Outcomes Researchers retrospectively analyzed patients hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV between 2016 and 2019 across seven transplant centers in the USA, Canada, and Australia. The median patient age was 61 years, and infection occurred a median of 14 months after transplantation. Hypoxic respiratory failure developed in 58.7% of patients, while 17.4% required mechanical ventilation. All-cause mortality within 90 days reached 7.7%. Patients requiring supplemental oxygen before infection had substantially greater odds of hypoxic respiratory failure (odds ratio [OR]: 4.81). Lower respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath, were also associated with increased odds (OR: 3.74). Older Age and Mechanical Ventilation Older age was associated with greater odds of requiring mechanical ventilation (OR: 1.06 per year), identifying an important factor when assessing hospitalized patients. Oral ribavirin treatment was associated with lower odds of mechanical ventilation (OR: 0.34). However, this association was not significant when oral and inhaled formulations were analyzed together. Oral ribavirin was also not associated with improved 90-day survival. These observational findings cannot establish treatment efficacy, particularly because prescribing decisions may have reflected differences in initial illness severity. Secondary Infections and Declining Lung Function Secondary bacterial or fungal infections developed in 33.5% of patients within 90 days. Mechanical ventilation was associated with greater odds of secondary infection (OR: 3.71). Among 61 patients with paired pulmonary function measurements, median forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) declined from 2.01 L before infection to 1.69 L afterward. Nearly half experienced reductions exceeding 10%. Graft rejection was observed in 12.3% of recipients following RSV infection. Mortality Findings Reinforce Clinical Vigilance Mechanical ventilation was strongly associated with 90-day mortality (hazard ratio: 7.79), emphasizing the severity of respiratory deterioration in this population. The retrospective design, limited number of deaths, and exclusive inclusion of hospitalized patients restrict generalizability. Outcomes also predate the availability of RSV vaccines. The findings support careful respiratory monitoring, recognition of secondary infections, and further investigation of preventive strategies to protect lung transplant recipients. Reference Mendoza MA et al. Risk factors for hypoxia, mechanical ventilation, and mortality in lung transplant recipients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus: A multicenter international cohort study. An international multicenter study of 155 adult lung transplant recipients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection identified clinical predictors of severe complications, highlighting the importance of early assessment and continued monitoring in this vulnerable population. RSV in Lung Transplant Recipients: Severe Outcomes. Researchers retrospectively analyzed patients hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV between 2016 and 2019 across seven transplant centers in the USA, Canada, and Australia. The median patient age was 61 years, and infection occurred a median of 14 months after transplantation. Hypoxic respiratory failure developed in 58.7% of patients, while 17.4% required mechanical ventilation. All-cause mortality within 90 days reached 7.7%. Patients requiring supplemental oxygen before infection had substantially greater odds of hypoxic respiratory failure (odds ratio [OR]: 4.81). Lower respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath, were also associated with increased odds (OR: 3.74). Older Age and Mechanical Ventilation. Older age was associated with greater odds of requiring mechanical ventilation (OR: 1.06 per year), identifying an important factor when assessing hospitalized patients. Oral ribavirin treatment was associated with lower odds of mechanical ventilation (OR: 0.34). However, this association was not significant when oral and inhaled formulations were analyzed together. Oral ribavirin was also not associated with improved 90-day survival. These observational findings cannot establish treatment efficacy, particularly because prescribing decisions may have reflected differences in initial illness severity. Secondary Infections and Declining Lung Function. Secondary bacterial or fungal infections developed in 33.5% of patients within 90 days. Mechanical ventilation was associated with greater odds of secondary infection (OR: 3.71). Among 61 patients with paired pulmonary function measurements, median forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) declined from 2.01 L before infection to 1.69 L afterward. Nearly half experienced reductions exceeding 10%. Graft rejection was observed in 12.3% of recipients following RSV infection. Mortality Findings Reinforce Clinical Vigilance. Mechanical ventilation was strongly associated with 90-day mortality (hazard ratio: 7.79), emphasizing the severity of respiratory deterioration in this population. The retrospective design, limited number of deaths, and exclusive inclusion of hospitalized patients restrict generalizability. Outcomes also predate the availability of RSV vaccines. The findings support careful respiratory monitoring, recognition of secondary infections, and further investigation of preventive strategies to protect lung transplant recipients.
